<p><b>Narendra Damodardas Modi</b> (<small>Gujarati:&#160;</small><span class="IPA nowrap" lang="gu-Latn-fonipa" title="Representation in the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA)"><a href="/wiki/Help:IPA/Gujarati" title="Help:IPA/Gujarati">[ˈnəɾendɾə<span class="wrap"> </span>dɑmodəɾˈdɑs<span class="wrap"> </span>ˈmodiː]</a></span>&#32;<span data-nosnippet="" id="ooui-php-1" class="ext-phonos ext-phonos-PhonosButton noexcerpt ext-phonos-PhonosButton-emptylabel oo-ui-widget oo-ui-widget-enabled oo-ui-buttonElement oo-ui-buttonElement-frameless oo-ui-iconElement oo-ui-buttonWidget" data-ooui="{&quot;_&quot;:&quot;mw.Phonos.PhonosButton&quot;,&quot;href&quot;:&quot;\/\/upload.wikimedia.org\/wikipedia\/commons\/transcoded\/3\/3b\/Narendra_Modi_pronouncing_his_name_at_swearing_in_2014.ogg\/Narendra_Modi_pronouncing_his_name_at_swearing_in_2014.ogg.mp3&quot;,&quot;rel&quot;:[&quot;nofollow&quot;],&quot;framed&quot;:false,&quot;icon&quot;:&quot;volumeUp&quot;,&quot;data&quot;:{&quot;ipa&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;text&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;lang&quot;:&quot;en&quot;,&quot;wikibase&quot;:&quot;&quot;,&quot;file&quot;:&quot;Narendra Modi pronouncing his name at swearing in 2014.ogg&quot;},&quot;classes&quot;:[&quot;ext-phonos&quot;,&quot;ext-phonos-PhonosButton&quot;,&quot;noexcerpt&quot;,&quot;ext-phonos-PhonosButton-emptylabel&quot;]}"><a role="button" tabindex="0" href="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/3/3b/Narendra_Modi_pronouncing_his_name_at_swearing_in_2014.ogg/Narendra_Modi_pronouncing_his_name_at_swearing_in_2014.ogg.mp3" rel="nofollow" aria-label="Play audio" class="oo-ui-buttonElement-button"><span class="oo-ui-iconElement-icon oo-ui-icon-volumeUp"></span><span class="oo-ui-labelElement-label"></span><span class="oo-ui-indicatorElement-indicator oo-ui-indicatorElement-noIndicator"></span></a></span><sup class="ext-phonos-attribution noexcerpt"><a href="/wiki/File:Narendra_Modi_pronouncing_his_name_at_swearing_in_2014.ogg" title="File:Narendra Modi pronouncing his name at swearing in 2014.ogg">i</a></sup>; born 17 September 1950)<sup id="cite_ref-foo_3-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-foo-3">&#91;b&#93;</a></sup> is an Indian politician who has served as the 14th <a href="/wiki/Prime_minister_of_India" class="mw-redirect" title="Prime minister of India">prime minister of India</a> since May 2014. Modi was the <a href="/wiki/Chief_Minister_of_Gujarat" class="mw-redirect" title="Chief Minister of Gujarat">Chief Minister of Gujarat</a> from 2001 to 2014 and is the <a href="/wiki/Member_of_Parliament,_Lok_Sabha" title="Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha">Member of Parliament</a> (MP) for <a href="/wiki/Varanasi_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)" class="mw-redirect" title="Varanasi (Lok Sabha constituency)">Varanasi</a>. He is a member of the <a href="/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party" title="Bharatiya Janata Party">Bharatiya Janata Party</a> (BJP) and of the <a href="/wiki/Rashtriya_Swayamsevak_Sangh" title="Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh">Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh</a> (RSS), a right-wing <a href="/wiki/Hindutva" title="Hindutva">Hindu nationalist</a> paramilitary volunteer organisation. He is the longest-serving prime minister from outside the <a href="/wiki/Indian_National_Congress" title="Indian National Congress">Indian National Congress</a>.
</p><p>Modi was born and raised in <a href="/wiki/Vadnagar" title="Vadnagar">Vadnagar</a> in northeastern <a href="/wiki/Gujarat" title="Gujarat">Gujarat</a>, where he completed his secondary education. He was introduced to the RSS at the age of eight. His account of helping his father sell tea at the Vadnagar railway station has not been reliably corroborated. At age 18, he was married to <a href="/wiki/Jashodaben_Modi" title="Jashodaben Modi">Jashodaben Modi</a>, whom he abandoned soon after, only publicly acknowledging her four decades later when legally required to do so. Modi became a full-time worker for the RSS in Gujarat in 1971. The RSS assigned him to the BJP in 1985 and he held several positions within the party hierarchy until 2001, rising to the rank of general secretary.<sup id="cite_ref-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-7">&#91;c&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2001, Modi was appointed Chief Minister of Gujarat and elected to the legislative assembly soon after. His administration is considered complicit in the <a href="/wiki/2002_Gujarat_riots" title="2002 Gujarat riots">2002 Gujarat riots</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-13" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-13">&#91;d&#93;</a></sup> and has been criticised for its management of the crisis. A little over 1,000 people were killed, according to official records, three-quarters of whom were Muslim; independent sources estimated 2,000 deaths, mostly Muslim.<sup id="cite_ref-unofficial-mortality_14-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-unofficial-mortality-14">&#91;10&#93;</a></sup> A Special Investigation Team appointed by the <a href="/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_India" title="Supreme Court of India">Supreme Court of India</a> in 2012 found no evidence to initiate prosecution proceedings against him.<sup id="cite_ref-17" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-17">&#91;e&#93;</a></sup> While his policies as chief minister, which were credited for encouraging economic growth, were praised, Modi's administration was criticised for failing to significantly improve health, poverty and education indices in the state.<sup id="cite_ref-18" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-18">&#91;f&#93;</a></sup> In the <a href="/wiki/2014_Indian_general_election" title="2014 Indian general election">2014 Indian general election</a>, Modi led the BJP to a <a href="/wiki/Lok_Sabha" title="Lok Sabha">parliamentary</a> majority, the first for a party since <a href="/wiki/1984_Indian_general_election" title="1984 Indian general election">1984</a>. His administration increased direct foreign investment; it reduced spending on healthcare, education, and social-welfare programmes.  Modi began a <a href="/wiki/Swachh_Bharat_Mission" title="Swachh Bharat Mission">high-profile sanitation campaign</a>, controversially initiated the <a href="/wiki/2016_Indian_banknote_demonetisation" title="2016 Indian banknote demonetisation">2016 demonetisation of high-denomination banknotes</a> and introduced the <a href="/wiki/Goods_and_Services_Tax_(India)" title="Goods and Services Tax (India)">Goods and Services Tax</a>, and weakened or abolished environmental and labour laws.
</p><p>Modi's administration launched the <a href="/wiki/2019_Balakot_airstrike" title="2019 Balakot airstrike">2019 Balakot airstrike</a> against an alleged terrorist training camp in Pakistan. The airstrike failed,<sup id="cite_ref-lalwani-tallo-2019_19-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-lalwani-tallo-2019-19">&#91;13&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-ian-hall-1_20-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ian-hall-1-20">&#91;14&#93;</a></sup> and the deaths of six Indian personnel to friendly fire was later revealed: but the action had nationalist appeal.<sup id="cite_ref-jaffrelot-2021-helicopter_21-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-jaffrelot-2021-helicopter-21">&#91;15&#93;</a></sup> Modi's party comfortably won the <a href="/wiki/2019_Indian_general_election" title="2019 Indian general election">2019 general election</a> which followed.<sup id="cite_ref-BS_Book_review_22-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-BS_Book_review-22">&#91;16&#93;</a></sup> In its second term, his administration <a href="/wiki/Revocation_of_the_special_status_of_Jammu_and_Kashmir" title="Revocation of the special status of Jammu and Kashmir">revoked the special status of Jammu and Kashmir</a>, an Indian-administred portion of the disputed <a href="/wiki/Kashmir" title="Kashmir">Kashmir</a> region,<sup id="cite_ref-britannica-jammu-kashmir_23-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-britannica-jammu-kashmir-23">&#91;17&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Osmańczyk2003_24-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Osmańczyk2003-24">&#91;18&#93;</a></sup> and introduced the <a href="/wiki/Citizenship_(Amendment)_Act,_2019" title="Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019">Citizenship Amendment Act</a>, prompting <a href="/wiki/Citizenship_Amendment_Act_protests" title="Citizenship Amendment Act protests">widespread protests</a>, and spurring the <a href="/wiki/2020_Delhi_riots" title="2020 Delhi riots">2020 Delhi riots</a> in which Muslims were brutalized and killed by Hindu mobs,<sup id="cite_ref-guardian-3-6-20_25-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-guardian-3-6-20-25">&#91;19&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-wamsley-frayer-npr-2020-2-26-3_26-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-wamsley-frayer-npr-2020-2-26-3-26">&#91;20&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-NYTimes-Analysis-March5_27-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NYTimes-Analysis-March5-27">&#91;21&#93;</a></sup> sometimes with the complicity of police forces controlled by the Modi administration.<sup id="cite_ref-28" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-28">&#91;22&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-29" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-29">&#91;23&#93;</a></sup> Three controversial <a href="/wiki/2020_Indian_agriculture_acts" title="2020 Indian agriculture acts">farm laws</a>, led to <a href="/wiki/2020%E2%80%932021_Indian_farmers%27_protest" title="2020–2021 Indian farmers&#39; protest">sit-ins</a> by farmers across the country, eventually causing their formal repeal. Modi oversaw India's response to the <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_India" title="COVID-19 pandemic in India">COVID-19 pandemic</a>, during which 4.7 million Indians died, according to the <a href="/wiki/World_Health_Organization" title="World Health Organization">World Health Organization</a>'s estimates.<sup id="cite_ref-WHO_estimate_30-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-WHO_estimate-30">&#91;24&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Biswas_2022_31-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Biswas_2022-31">&#91;25&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Under Modi's tenure, India has experienced <a href="/wiki/Democratic_backsliding" title="Democratic backsliding">democratic backsliding</a>, or the weakening of democratic institutions, <a href="/wiki/Individual_rights" class="mw-redirect" title="Individual rights">individual rights</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_expression" class="mw-redirect" title="Freedom of expression">freedom of expression</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-welzel-etal-2019_32-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-welzel-etal-2019-32">&#91;26&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-chidambaram-2022_33-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-chidambaram-2022-33">&#91;27&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-lo9_39-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-lo9-39">&#91;g&#93;</a></sup> As prime minister, he has received <a href="/wiki/Opinion_polling_on_the_Narendra_Modi_premiership" title="Opinion polling on the Narendra Modi premiership">consistently high approval ratings</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:0_40-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-40">&#91;33&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-41" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-41">&#91;34&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-42" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-42">&#91;35&#93;</a></sup> Modi has been described as engineering a political realignment towards <a href="/wiki/Right-wing_politics" title="Right-wing politics">right-wing politics</a>. He remains a controversial figure domestically and internationally, over his Hindu nationalist beliefs and handling of the 2002 Gujarat riots, which have been cited as evidence of a majoritarian and exclusionary social agenda.<sup id="cite_ref-49" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-49">&#91;h&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<meta property="mw:PageProp/toc" />
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Early_life_and_education">Early life and education</span></h2>
<p>Narendra Damodardas Modi was born on 17 September 1950 to a <a href="/wiki/Gujarati_people" title="Gujarati people">Gujarati</a> <a href="/wiki/Hindu" class="mw-redirect" title="Hindu">Hindu</a> family of grocers in <a href="/wiki/Vadnagar" title="Vadnagar">Vadnagar</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mehsana_district" title="Mehsana district">Mehsana district</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bombay_State" title="Bombay State">Bombay State</a> (present-day <a href="/wiki/Gujarat" title="Gujarat">Gujarat</a>). He was the third of six children born to Damodardas Mulchand Modi (<abbr title="circa">c.</abbr><span style="white-space:nowrap;">&#8201;1915–1989</span>) and Hiraben Modi (1923–2022).<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMarino201413,_15,_29–30,_74_50-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarino201413,_15,_29–30,_74-50">&#91;42&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-foo_3-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-foo-3">&#91;b&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-51" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-51">&#91;43&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>According to Modi, as a child, he had to work in his father's tea shop on the platform of <a href="/wiki/Vadnagar_railway_station" title="Vadnagar railway station">Vadnagar railway station</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-chatterji-Hansen-Jaffrelot-tea_52-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-chatterji-Hansen-Jaffrelot-tea-52">&#91;44&#93;</a></sup> but the evidence of his neighbours does not entirely corroborate this statement.<sup id="cite_ref-roberts-tea-stall_53-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-roberts-tea-stall-53">&#91;45&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-adam-roberts-economist_54-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-adam-roberts-economist-54">&#91;46&#93;</a></sup> During a protest against the government, his brother, Prahlad Modi, contradicted that he ever sold tea. According to him, his father had brought up six of his children by selling tea and people were making a big mistake by calling the Prime Minister a "chai wala" (tea seller).<sup id="cite_ref-55" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-55">&#91;47&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Modi completed his <a href="/wiki/Higher_Secondary_Examination" class="mw-redirect" title="Higher Secondary Examination">higher secondary education</a> in Vadnagar in 1967; his teachers described him as an average student and a keen, gifted debater with an interest in theatre.<sup id="cite_ref-Jose_Caravan_56-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jose_Caravan-56">&#91;48&#93;</a></sup> He preferred playing larger-than-life characters in theatrical productions, which has influenced his political image.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMukhopadhyay201382_57-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMukhopadhyay201382-57">&#91;49&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-58" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-58">&#91;50&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>When Modi was eight years old, he was introduced to the <a href="/wiki/Rashtriya_Swayamsevak_Sangh" title="Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh">Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh</a> (RSS) and began attending its local <i>shakhas</i> (training sessions). There, he met <a href="/wiki/Lakshmanrao_Inamdar" title="Lakshmanrao Inamdar">Lakshmanrao Inamdar</a>, who inducted Modi as a <i><a href="/wiki/Swayamsevak_(RSS)" class="mw-redirect" title="Swayamsevak (RSS)">balswayamsevak</a></i> (junior cadet) in the RSS and became his political mentor.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMarino201424_59-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarino201424-59">&#91;51&#93;</a></sup> While Modi was training with the RSS, he also met Vasant Gajendragadkar and Nathalal Jaghda, <a href="/wiki/Bharatiya_Jana_Sangh" title="Bharatiya Jana Sangh">Bharatiya Jana Sangh</a> leaders who in 1980 helped found the BJP's Gujarat unit.<sup id="cite_ref-Pathak_TNN_60-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Pathak_TNN-60">&#91;52&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In a custom traditional to Narendra Modi's caste, his family arranged a betrothal to <a href="/wiki/Jashodaben_Chimanlal_Modi" class="mw-redirect" title="Jashodaben Chimanlal Modi">Jashodaben Chimanlal Modi</a>, leading to their marriage when she was 17 and he was 18.<sup id="cite_ref-gowen1_61-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-gowen1-61">&#91;53&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-shultz-kumar2_62-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-shultz-kumar2-62">&#91;54&#93;</a></sup> Soon afterwards, he abandoned his wife,<sup id="cite_ref-gowen2_63-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-gowen2-63">&#91;55&#93;</a></sup> and left home. The couple never divorced but the marriage was not in his public pronouncements for many decades.<sup id="cite_ref-shultz-kumar2_62-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-shultz-kumar2-62">&#91;54&#93;</a></sup> In April 2014, shortly before the national election in which he gained power, Modi publicly affirmed he was married and that his spouse was Jashodaben.<sup id="cite_ref-CNN1_64-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CNN1-64">&#91;56&#93;</a></sup> The marriage was sexless and Modi kept it secret because he would not have been able to become a <i>pracharak</i> in the puritanical RSS.<sup id="cite_ref-IT13092013_65-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-IT13092013-65">&#91;57&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMukhopadhyay2013A_time_of_difference_66-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMukhopadhyay2013A_time_of_difference-66">&#91;58&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Modi spent the following two years travelling across northern and north-eastern India.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMarino201425_67-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarino201425-67">&#91;59&#93;</a></sup> In interviews, he has described visiting Hindu ashrams founded by <a href="/wiki/Swami_Vivekananda" title="Swami Vivekananda">Swami Vivekananda</a>: the <a href="/wiki/Belur_Math" title="Belur Math">Belur Math</a> near <a href="/wiki/Kolkata" title="Kolkata">Kolkata</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Advaita_Ashrama" title="Advaita Ashrama">Advaita Ashrama</a> in <a href="/wiki/Almora" title="Almora">Almora</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Ramakrishna_Mission" title="Ramakrishna Mission">Ramakrishna Mission</a> in <a href="/wiki/Rajkot" title="Rajkot">Rajkot</a>. His stays at each ashram were brief because he lacked the required college education.<sup id="cite_ref-68" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-68">&#91;60&#93;</a></sup> Vivekananda has had a large influence in Modi's life.<sup id="cite_ref-ts0716_69-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ts0716-69">&#91;61&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In mid 1968, Modi reached <a href="/wiki/Belur_Math" title="Belur Math">Belur Math</a> but was turned away, after which he visited <a href="/wiki/Calcutta" class="mw-redirect" title="Calcutta">Calcutta</a>, <a href="/wiki/West_Bengal" title="West Bengal">West Bengal</a> and <a href="/wiki/Assam" title="Assam">Assam</a>, stopping in <a href="/wiki/Siliguri" title="Siliguri">Siliguri</a> and <a href="/wiki/Guwahati" title="Guwahati">Guwahati</a>. He then went to the <a href="/wiki/Ramakrishna_Ashram_Marg_metro_station" title="Ramakrishna Ashram Marg metro station">Ramakrishna Ashram</a> in <a href="/wiki/Almora" title="Almora">Almora</a>, where he was again rejected, before returning to <a href="/wiki/Gujarat" title="Gujarat">Gujarat</a> via <a href="/wiki/Delhi" title="Delhi">Delhi</a> and <a href="/wiki/Rajasthan" title="Rajasthan">Rajasthan</a> in 1968 to 1969. In either late 1969 or early 1970, he returned to Vadnagar for a brief visit before leaving again for <a href="/wiki/Ahmedabad" title="Ahmedabad">Ahmedabad</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMarino201426–29_70-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarino201426–29-70">&#91;62&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGuha2007491–492Panda201696Mahurkar20177–9_71-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGuha2007491–492Panda201696Mahurkar20177–9-71">&#91;63&#93;</a></sup> where he lived with his uncle and worked in his uncle's <a href="/wiki/Cafeteria" title="Cafeteria">canteen</a> at <a href="/wiki/Gujarat_State_Road_Transport_Corporation" title="Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation">Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMukhopadhyay2013131,_138_72-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMukhopadhyay2013131,_138-72">&#91;64&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In Ahmedabad, Modi renewed his acquaintance with Inamdar, who was based at the Hedgewar Bhavan (RSS headquarters) in the city.<sup id="cite_ref-vakilsaheb_73-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-vakilsaheb-73">&#91;65&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-livemint-modi-growth_74-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-livemint-modi-growth-74">&#91;66&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMarino201435_75-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarino201435-75">&#91;67&#93;</a></sup> Modi's first-known political activity as an adult was in 1971 when he joined a <a href="/wiki/Jana_Sangh" class="mw-redirect" title="Jana Sangh">Jana Sangh</a> Satyagraha in Delhi led by <a href="/wiki/Atal_Bihari_Vajpayee" title="Atal Bihari Vajpayee">Atal Bihari Vajpayee</a> to enlist to fight in the <a href="/wiki/Bangladesh_Liberation_War" title="Bangladesh Liberation War">Bangladesh Liberation War</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-76" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-76">&#91;68&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-77" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-77">&#91;69&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Indira_Gandhi" title="Indira Gandhi">Indira Gandhi</a>-led central government prohibited open support for the <a href="/wiki/Mukti_Bahini" title="Mukti Bahini">Mukti Bahini</a>; according to Modi, he was briefly held in <a href="/wiki/Tihar_Jail" title="Tihar Jail">Tihar Jail</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-78" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-78">&#91;70&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-tribune_79-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-tribune-79">&#91;71&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-80" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-80">&#91;72&#93;</a></sup> After the <a href="/wiki/Indo-Pakistani_War_of_1971" title="Indo-Pakistani War of 1971">Indo-Pakistani War of 1971</a>, Modi left his uncle's employ and became a full-time <i><a href="/wiki/Pracharak" class="mw-redirect" title="Pracharak">pracharak</a></i> (campaigner) for the RSS,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMukhopadhyay2013138_81-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMukhopadhyay2013138-81">&#91;73&#93;</a></sup> working under Inamdar.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMarino201435–40_82-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarino201435–40-82">&#91;74&#93;</a></sup> Shortly before the war, Modi took part in a non-violent protest in New Delhi against the Indian government, for which he was arrested; because of this arrest, Inamdar decided to mentor Modi.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMarino201435–40_82-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarino201435–40-82">&#91;74&#93;</a></sup>  According to Modi, he was part of a Satyagraha that led to a political war.<sup id="cite_ref-tribune_79-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-tribune-79">&#91;71&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-85" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-85">&#91;i&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 1978, Modi received a <a href="/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts" title="Bachelor of Arts">Bachelor of Arts</a> (BA) degree in political science from the <a href="/wiki/School_of_Open_Learning" title="School of Open Learning">School of Open Learning</a><sup id="cite_ref-SOL_86-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-SOL-86">&#91;77&#93;</a></sup> at the <a href="/wiki/Delhi_University" title="Delhi University">Delhi University</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-IT13092013_65-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-IT13092013-65">&#91;57&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-87" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-87">&#91;78&#93;</a></sup> In 1983, he received a <a href="/wiki/Master_of_Arts" title="Master of Arts">Master of Arts</a> (MA) degree in political science from <a href="/wiki/Gujarat_University" title="Gujarat University">Gujarat University</a>, graduating with a <a href="/wiki/Academic_grading_in_India" title="Academic grading in India">first class</a><sup id="cite_ref-88" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-88">&#91;79&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-89" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-89">&#91;80&#93;</a></sup> as an external <a href="/wiki/Distance_education" title="Distance education">distance learning</a> student.<sup id="cite_ref-GU_Modi_90-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-GU_Modi-90">&#91;81&#93;</a></sup> There is a controversy surrounding the authenticity of his BA and MA degrees.<sup id="cite_ref-91" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-91">&#91;82&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-92" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-92">&#91;83&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-96" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-96">&#91;j&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Early_political_career">Early political career</span></h2>
<p>In June 1975, Prime Minister <a href="/wiki/Indira_Gandhi" title="Indira Gandhi">Indira Gandhi</a> declared a <a href="/wiki/The_Emergency_(India)" title="The Emergency (India)">state of emergency</a> in India that lasted until 1977. During this period, known as "the Emergency", many of her political opponents were jailed and opposition groups were banned.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGuha2007493–494_97-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGuha2007493–494-97">&#91;87&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEKochanekHardgrave2007205_98-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKochanekHardgrave2007205-98">&#91;88&#93;</a></sup> Modi was appointed general secretary of the "Gujarat Lok Sangharsh Samiti", an RSS committee co-ordinating opposition to the Emergency in Gujarat. Shortly afterwards, the RSS was banned.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMarino201436–40_99-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarino201436–40-99">&#91;89&#93;</a></sup> Modi was forced to go underground in Gujarat and frequently travelled in disguise to avoid arrest, once dressing as a monk and once as a <a href="/wiki/Sikh" class="mw-redirect" title="Sikh">Sikh</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMarino201471–74Natarajan_and_Pooja201998–101_100-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarino201471–74Natarajan_and_Pooja201998–101-100">&#91;90&#93;</a></sup> He became involved in the printing of pamphlets opposing the government, sending them to Delhi and organising demonstrations.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMarino201443_101-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarino201443-101">&#91;91&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMukhopadhyay2013150_102-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMukhopadhyay2013150-102">&#91;92&#93;</a></sup> He was also involved with creating a network of safe houses for individuals who were wanted by the government, and in raising funds for political refugees and activists.<sup id="cite_ref-103" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-103">&#91;93&#93;</a></sup> During this period, Modi wrote a <a href="/wiki/Gujarati_language" title="Gujarati language">Gujarati-language</a> book titled <i>Sangharsh Ma Gujarat</i> (<i>In the Struggles of Gujarat</i>), which describes events during the Emergency.<sup id="cite_ref-Aakar-PoetModi_104-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Aakar-PoetModi-104">&#91;94&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-105" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-105">&#91;95&#93;</a></sup> While in this role, Modi met trade unionist and socialist activist <a href="/wiki/George_Fernandes" title="George Fernandes">George Fernandes</a> and several other national political figures.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMarino201438–43,_46–50_106-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarino201438–43,_46–50-106">&#91;96&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Modi became an RSS <i>sambhag pracharak</i> (regional organiser) in 1978, overseeing activities in <a href="/wiki/Surat" title="Surat">Surat</a> and <a href="/wiki/Vadodara" title="Vadodara">Vadodara</a>, and in 1979, he went to work for the RSS in Delhi, where he researched and wrote the RSS's history of the Emergency. Shortly after, he returned to Gujarat and in 1985, the RSS assigned him to the BJP. In 1987, Modi helped organise the BJP's campaign in the Ahmedabad municipal election, which the party won comfortably; according to biographers, Modi's planning was responsible for the win.<sup id="cite_ref-107" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-107">&#91;97&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMarino201445–48,_54–59_108-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarino201445–48,_54–59-108">&#91;98&#93;</a></sup> After <a href="/wiki/L._K._Advani" title="L. K. Advani">L. K. Advani</a> became president of the BJP in 1986, the RSS decided to place its members in important positions within the party; Modi's work during the Ahmedabad election led to his selection for this role. Modi was elected organising secretary of the BJP's Gujarat unit later in 1987.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGuha2007Marino201456Panda2016fontcoverRao2020228_109-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGuha2007Marino201456Panda2016fontcoverRao2020228-109">&#91;99&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Narendra_Modi_and_Prime_Minister_Atal_Bihari_Vajpayee_in_New_Delhi_in_October_12,_2001.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Narendra_Modi_and_Prime_Minister_Atal_Bihari_Vajpayee_in_New_Delhi_in_October_12%2C_2001.jpg/240px-Narendra_Modi_and_Prime_Minister_Atal_Bihari_Vajpayee_in_New_Delhi_in_October_12%2C_2001.jpg" decoding="async" width="240" height="178" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/0f/Narendra_Modi_and_Prime_Minister_Atal_Bihari_Vajpayee_in_New_Delhi_in_October_12%2C_2001.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="269" data-file-height="200" /></a><figcaption>Modi with <a href="/wiki/Atal_Bihari_Vajpayee" title="Atal Bihari Vajpayee">Atal Bihari Vajpayee</a> in <abbr title="circa">c.</abbr><span style="white-space:nowrap;">&#8201;2001</span></figcaption></figure>
<p>Modi rose within the party and was named a member of its National Election Committee in 1990, helping organise Advani's <a href="/wiki/Ram_Rath_Yatra" title="Ram Rath Yatra">Ram Rath Yatra</a> in 1990 and <a href="/wiki/Murli_Manohar_Joshi" title="Murli Manohar Joshi">Murli Manohar Joshi</a>'s 1991–1992 <i><a href="/wiki/Ekta_Yatra" title="Ekta Yatra">Ekta Yatra</a></i> (Journey for Unity).<sup id="cite_ref-Jose_Caravan_56-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jose_Caravan-56">&#91;48&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMukhopadhyay201368–69_110-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMukhopadhyay201368–69-110">&#91;100&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMarino201460–63_111-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarino201460–63-111">&#91;101&#93;</a></sup> Modi took a brief break from politics in 1992 to establish a school in Ahmedabad, and due to friction with <a href="/wiki/Shankersinh_Vaghela" title="Shankersinh Vaghela">Shankersinh Vaghela</a>, a BJP MP from Gujarat.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMarino201460–63_111-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarino201460–63-111">&#91;101&#93;</a></sup> Modi returned to electoral politics in 1994, partly at the insistence of Advani; as party secretary, Modi's electoral strategy was considered central to the BJP victory in the <a href="/wiki/1995_Gujarat_Legislative_Assembly_election" title="1995 Gujarat Legislative Assembly election">1995 state assembly election</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-112" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-112">&#91;102&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-113" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-113">&#91;103&#93;</a></sup> In November of that year, Modi was appointed BJP national secretary and transferred to New Delhi, where he assumed responsibility for party activities in <a href="/wiki/Haryana" title="Haryana">Haryana</a> and <a href="/wiki/Himachal_Pradesh" title="Himachal Pradesh">Himachal Pradesh</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-114" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-114">&#91;104&#93;</a></sup> The following year, Shankersinh Vaghela, a prominent BJP leader from Gujarat, defected to the <a href="/wiki/Indian_National_Congress" title="Indian National Congress">Indian National Congress</a> (Congress) after losing his parliamentary seat in the Lok Sabha election.<sup id="cite_ref-Jose_Caravan_56-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jose_Caravan-56">&#91;48&#93;</a></sup> Modi, who was on the selection committee for the <a href="/wiki/1998_Gujarat_Legislative_Assembly_election" title="1998 Gujarat Legislative Assembly election">1998 Gujarat Legislative Assembly election</a>, favoured supporters of BJP leader <a href="/wiki/Keshubhai_Patel" title="Keshubhai Patel">Keshubhai Patel</a> over those supporting Vaghela to end factional division in the party. His strategy was credited as central to the BJP winning an overall majority in the 1998 election,<sup id="cite_ref-Venkatesan_Frontline_115-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Venkatesan_Frontline-115">&#91;105&#93;</a></sup> and Modi was promoted to BJP general secretary (organisation) in May of that year.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMarino201478–79Mukhopadhyay201378–95_116-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarino201478–79Mukhopadhyay201378–95-116">&#91;106&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Chief_Minister_of_Gujarat">Chief Minister of Gujarat</span></h2>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Taking_office">Taking office</span></h3>
<p>In 2001, <a href="/wiki/Keshubhai_Patel" title="Keshubhai Patel">Keshubhai Patel</a>'s health was failing and the BJP lost a few state assembly seats in <a href="/wiki/By-election" title="By-election">by-elections</a>. Allegations of abuse of power, corruption and poor administration were made, and Patel's standing had been damaged by his administration's handling of the <a href="/wiki/2001_Gujarat_earthquake" title="2001 Gujarat earthquake">earthquake in Bhuj in 2001</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Venkatesan_Frontline_115-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Venkatesan_Frontline-115">&#91;105&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Phadnis_BS_117-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Phadnis_BS-117">&#91;107&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-118" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-118">&#91;108&#93;</a></sup> The BJP national leadership sought a new candidate for the chief ministership, and Modi, who had expressed misgivings about Patel's administration, was chosen as a replacement.<sup id="cite_ref-Jose_Caravan_56-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jose_Caravan-56">&#91;48&#93;</a></sup> Advani did not want to ostracise Patel and was concerned about Modi's lack of experience in government. Modi declined an offer to become Patel's <a href="/wiki/List_of_deputy_chief_ministers_of_Gujarat" title="List of deputy chief ministers of Gujarat">deputy chief minister</a>, telling Advani and <a href="/wiki/Atal_Bihari_Vajpayee" title="Atal Bihari Vajpayee">Atal Bihari Vajpayee</a> he was "going to be fully responsible for Gujarat or not at all". On 3 October 2001, Modi replaced Patel as Chief Minister of Gujarat with the responsibility of preparing the BJP for the upcoming December 2002 election.<sup id="cite_ref-119" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-119">&#91;109&#93;</a></sup> On 7 October, Modi was sworn in<sup id="cite_ref-120" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-120">&#91;110&#93;</a></sup> and he entered the Gujarat state legislature on 24 February 2002 after winning a by-election in <a href="/wiki/Rajkot_West" class="mw-redirect" title="Rajkot West">Rajkot II</a> constituency, defeating Ashwin Mehta of the INC.<sup id="cite_ref-121" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-121">&#91;111&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="2002_Gujarat_riots">2002 Gujarat riots</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/2002_Gujarat_riots" title="2002 Gujarat riots">2002 Gujarat riots</a></div>
<p>On 27 February 2002, a train with several hundred passengers <a href="/wiki/Godhra_train_burning" title="Godhra train burning">burned near Godhra</a>, killing approximately 60 people.<sup id="cite_ref-124" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-124">&#91;k&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-leaders_failed_2021_11_15_dhaka_tribune_125-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-leaders_failed_2021_11_15_dhaka_tribune-125">&#91;114&#93;</a></sup> The train carried a large number of Hindu pilgrims who were returning from <a href="/wiki/Ayodhya" title="Ayodhya">Ayodhya</a> after a religious ceremony at the site of the demolished <a href="/wiki/Babri_Masjid" title="Babri Masjid">Babri Masjid</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Communal_Riots_126-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Communal_Riots-126">&#91;115&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-BBC1_127-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-BBC1-127">&#91;116&#93;</a></sup> In a public statement, Modi said local Muslims were responsible for the incident.<sup id="cite_ref-Shani_10-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Shani-10">&#91;7&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Communal_Riots_126-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Communal_Riots-126">&#91;115&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Murphy_2010_128-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Murphy_2010-128">&#91;117&#93;</a></sup> The next day, the <a href="/wiki/Vishwa_Hindu_Parishad" class="mw-redirect" title="Vishwa Hindu Parishad">Vishwa Hindu Parishad</a> called for a <i><a href="/wiki/Bandh" title="Bandh">bandh</a></i> (general strike) across the state.<sup id="cite_ref-articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com_129-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com-129">&#91;118&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Curfew_imposed_in_26_cities_130-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Curfew_imposed_in_26_cities-130">&#91;119&#93;</a></sup> Riots began during the <i>bandh</i> and <a href="/wiki/Anti-Muslim_violence_in_India" class="mw-redirect" title="Anti-Muslim violence in India">anti-Muslim violence</a> spread through Gujarat.<sup id="cite_ref-Communal_Riots_126-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Communal_Riots-126">&#91;115&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com_129-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com-129">&#91;118&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Curfew_imposed_in_26_cities_130-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Curfew_imposed_in_26_cities-130">&#91;119&#93;</a></sup> The government's decision to move the bodies of the train victims from Godhra to Ahmedabad further inflamed the violence.<sup id="cite_ref-Communal_Riots_126-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Communal_Riots-126">&#91;115&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-131" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-131">&#91;120&#93;</a></sup> The state government later stated 790 Muslims and 254 Hindus were killed during the riots;<sup id="cite_ref-BBC1_127-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-BBC1-127">&#91;116&#93;</a></sup> independent sources put the death toll at over 2,000,<sup id="cite_ref-Communal_Riots_126-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Communal_Riots-126">&#91;115&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-leaders_failed_2021_11_15_dhaka_tribune_125-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-leaders_failed_2021_11_15_dhaka_tribune-125">&#91;114&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-132" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-132">&#91;121&#93;</a></sup> the vast majority of them Muslims.<sup id="cite_ref-leaders_failed_2021_11_15_dhaka_tribune_125-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-leaders_failed_2021_11_15_dhaka_tribune-125">&#91;114&#93;</a></sup> Approximately 150,000 people were driven to refugee camps.<sup id="cite_ref-Brass_133-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Brass-133">&#91;122&#93;</a></sup> Numerous women and children were among the victims; the violence included mass rapes and mutilation of women.<sup id="cite_ref-The_Clash_Within_9-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-The_Clash_Within-9">&#91;6&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-134" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-134">&#91;123&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Scholars consider the <a href="/wiki/Government_of_Gujarat" title="Government of Gujarat">Government of Gujarat</a> to have been complicit in the riots,<sup id="cite_ref-Shani_10-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Shani-10">&#91;7&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-135" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-135">&#91;124&#93;</a></sup> and it has received much criticism for its handling of the situation;<sup id="cite_ref-NYT_136-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NYT-136">&#91;125&#93;</a></sup> some scholars explicitly blame Modi.<sup id="cite_ref-The_Clash_Within_9-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-The_Clash_Within-9">&#91;6&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-137" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-137">&#91;126&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-138" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-138">&#91;127&#93;</a></sup> The Modi government imposed a curfew in 26 major cities, issued shoot-at-sight orders and called for the army to patrol the streets; these measured failed to prevent the violence from escalating.<sup id="cite_ref-articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com_129-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com-129">&#91;118&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Curfew_imposed_in_26_cities_130-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Curfew_imposed_in_26_cities-130">&#91;119&#93;</a></sup> The president of the state unit of the BJP expressed support for the <i>bandh</i> despite such actions being illegal at the time.<sup id="cite_ref-Shani_10-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Shani-10">&#91;7&#93;</a></sup> State officials later prevented riot victims from leaving the refugee camps, which were often unable to meet the needs of those living there.<sup id="cite_ref-Hampton_2002_139-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Hampton_2002-139">&#91;128&#93;</a></sup> Muslim victims of the riots were subjected to further discrimination when the state government announced their compensation would be half that offered to Hindu victims; this decision was later reversed after the issue was taken to court.<sup id="cite_ref-Gujarat_Model_140-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Gujarat_Model-140">&#91;129&#93;</a></sup> During the riots, police officers often did not intervene in situations where they were able.<sup id="cite_ref-The_Clash_Within_9-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-The_Clash_Within-9">&#91;6&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Murphy_2010_128-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Murphy_2010-128">&#91;117&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Gujarat_2002_141-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Gujarat_2002-141">&#91;130&#93;</a></sup> Several scholars have described the violence as a <a href="/wiki/Pogrom" title="Pogrom">pogrom</a> and others have called it an example of <a href="/wiki/State_terrorism" title="State terrorism">state terrorism</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-142" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-142">&#91;131&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Pandey_2005_143-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Pandey_2005-143">&#91;132&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Baruah_2012_144-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Baruah_2012-144">&#91;133&#93;</a></sup> According to <a href="/wiki/Martha_Nussbaum" title="Martha Nussbaum">Martha Nussbaum</a>; "There is by now a broad consensus that the Gujarat violence was a form of ethnic cleansing, that in many ways it was premeditated, and that it was carried out with the complicity of the state government and officers of the law".<sup id="cite_ref-The_Clash_Within_9-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-The_Clash_Within-9">&#91;6&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Modi's personal involvement in the 2002 events has continued to be debated. During the riots, he said; "What is happening is a chain of action and reaction".<sup id="cite_ref-The_Clash_Within_9-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-The_Clash_Within-9">&#91;6&#93;</a></sup> Later in 2002, Modi said the way in which he had handled the media was his only regret regarding the episode.<sup id="cite_ref-145" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-145">&#91;134&#93;</a></sup> In March 2008, the <a href="/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_India" title="Supreme Court of India">Supreme Court of India</a> reopened several cases related to the riots, including that of the <a href="/wiki/Gulbarg_Society_massacre" title="Gulbarg Society massacre">Gulbarg Society massacre</a>, and established a <a href="/wiki/Special_Investigation_Team_(India)" title="Special Investigation Team (India)">Special Investigation Team</a> (SIT) to look into the issue.<sup id="cite_ref-NYT_136-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NYT-136">&#91;125&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-ZakiavsModi-timeline_146-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ZakiavsModi-timeline-146">&#91;135&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-NHRCvsGujarat-2009-judgment_147-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NHRCvsGujarat-2009-judgment-147">&#91;136&#93;</a></sup> In response to a petition from Zakia Jafri, the widow of <a href="/wiki/Ehsan_Jafri" title="Ehsan Jafri">Ehsan Jafri</a>, who was killed in the Gulbarg Society massacre, in April 2009, the court also asked the SIT to investigate Modi's complicity in the killings.<sup id="cite_ref-ZakiavsModi-timeline_146-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ZakiavsModi-timeline-146">&#91;135&#93;</a></sup> The SIT questioned Modi in March 2010; in May, it presented to the court a report finding no evidence against him.<sup id="cite_ref-ZakiavsModi-timeline_146-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ZakiavsModi-timeline-146">&#91;135&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-148" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-148">&#91;137&#93;</a></sup> In July 2011, the court-appointed <i><a href="/wiki/Amicus_curiae" title="Amicus curiae">amicus curiae</a></i> <a href="/wiki/Raju_Ramachandran" title="Raju Ramachandran">Raju Ramachandran</a> submitted his final report to the court. Contrary to the SIT's position, Ramachandran said Modi could be prosecuted based on the available evidence.<sup id="cite_ref-hindu-raju-report_149-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-hindu-raju-report-149">&#91;138&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-150" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-150">&#91;139&#93;</a></sup> The Supreme Court sent the matter to the magistrate's court. The SIT examined Ramachandran's report, and in March 2012 submitted its final report, asking for the case to be closed. Zakia Jafri filed a protest petition in response. In December 2013, the magistrate's court rejected the protest petition, accepting the SIT's finding there was no evidence against Modi.<sup id="cite_ref-2013_Clean_chit_151-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2013_Clean_chit-151">&#91;140&#93;</a></sup> In 2022, the Supreme Court dismissed a petition by Zakia Jafri in which she challenged the clean chit given to Modi in the riots by the SIT, and upheld previous rulings that no evidence against him was found.<sup id="cite_ref-152" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-152">&#91;141&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-153" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-153">&#91;142&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-154" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-154">&#91;143&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Later_terms_as_Chief_Minister">Later terms as Chief Minister</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/2002_Gujarat_Legislative_Assembly_election" title="2002 Gujarat Legislative Assembly election">2002 Gujarat Legislative Assembly election</a></div>
<p>Following the violence, calls for Modi to resign as chief minister were made from politicians within and outside the state, including leaders of <a href="/wiki/Dravida_Munnetra_Kazhagam" title="Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam">Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Telugu_Desam_Party" title="Telugu Desam Party">Telugu Desam Party</a>—partners in the BJP-led <a href="/wiki/National_Democratic_Alliance" title="National Democratic Alliance">National Democratic Alliance</a> coalition—and opposition parties stalled Parliament over the issue.<sup id="cite_ref-155" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-155">&#91;144&#93;</a></sup> Modi submitted his resignation at the April 2002 BJP national executive meeting in Goa but it was not accepted.<sup id="cite_ref-156" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-156">&#91;145&#93;</a></sup> Despite opposition from the election commissioner, who said a number of voters were still displaced, Modi succeeded in advancing the election to December 2002.<sup id="cite_ref-Jaffrelot_T&amp;NM_157-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jaffrelot_T&amp;NM-157">&#91;146&#93;</a></sup> In the election, the BJP won 127 seats in the 182-member assembly.<sup id="cite_ref-auto_158-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto-158">&#91;147&#93;</a></sup> Modi made significant use of anti-Muslim rhetoric during his campaign,<sup id="cite_ref-India_Review_159-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-India_Review-159">&#91;148&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Brasted_160-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Brasted-160">&#91;149&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-161" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-161">&#91;150&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-162" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-162">&#91;151&#93;</a></sup> and the BJP profited from religious polarisation among voters.<sup id="cite_ref-Jaffrelot_T&amp;NM_157-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jaffrelot_T&amp;NM-157">&#91;146&#93;</a></sup> Modi framed the criticism of his government for human rights violations as an attack upon Gujarati pride,<sup id="cite_ref-Bobbio_8-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bobbio-8">&#91;5&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-India_Review_159-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-India_Review-159">&#91;148&#93;</a></sup> a strategy that led to the BJP winning 127 of the 182<sup id="cite_ref-auto_158-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto-158">&#91;147&#93;</a></sup> seats—a two-thirds majority—in the state assembly.<sup id="cite_ref-Bobbio_8-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bobbio-8">&#91;5&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-India_Review_159-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-India_Review-159">&#91;148&#93;</a></sup> He won Maninagar constituency, defeating Congress candidate Yatin Oza.<sup id="cite_ref-163" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-163">&#91;152&#93;</a></sup> On 22 December 2002, Modi was sworn in for a second term.<sup id="cite_ref-164" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-164">&#91;153&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>During Modi's second term, the government's rhetoric shifted from <a href="/wiki/Hindutva" title="Hindutva">Hindutva</a> to Gujarat's economic development.<sup id="cite_ref-Phadnis_BS_117-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Phadnis_BS-117">&#91;107&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Bobbio_8-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bobbio-8">&#91;5&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-India_Review_159-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-India_Review-159">&#91;148&#93;</a></sup> He curtailed the influence of <a href="/wiki/Sangh_Parivar" title="Sangh Parivar">Sangh Parivar</a> organisations such as <a href="/wiki/Bharatiya_Kisan_Sangh" title="Bharatiya Kisan Sangh">Bharatiya Kisan Sangh</a> (BKS) and <a href="/wiki/Vishva_Hindu_Parishad" title="Vishva Hindu Parishad">Vishva Hindu Parishad</a> (VHP).<sup id="cite_ref-Umat_TNN_165-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Umat_TNN-165">&#91;154&#93;</a></sup> When the BKS staged a farmers' demonstration, Modi ordered the BKS's eviction from state-provided houses, and his decision to demolish 200 illegal temples in <a href="/wiki/Gandhinagar" title="Gandhinagar">Gandhinagar</a> deepened the rift with the VHP.<sup id="cite_ref-Umat_TNN_165-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Umat_TNN-165">&#91;154&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-166" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-166">&#91;155&#93;</a></sup> Modi retained connections with some Hindu nationalists. He wrote a foreword to a 2014 textbook by <a href="/wiki/Dinanath_Batra" title="Dinanath Batra">Dinanath Batra</a>, which made the unscientific claim that ancient India possessed technologies including <a href="/wiki/Test-tube_babies" class="mw-redirect" title="Test-tube babies">test-tube babies</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-testtubes_167-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-testtubes-167">&#91;156&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Manor_168-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Manor-168">&#91;157&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Modi's relationship with Muslims continued to attract criticism. Prime Minister <a href="/wiki/Atal_Bihari_Vajpayee" title="Atal Bihari Vajpayee">Atal Bihari Vajpayee</a> distanced himself, reaching out to North Indian Muslims before the <a href="/wiki/2004_Indian_general_election" title="2004 Indian general election">2004 Indian general election</a>, following which, Vajpayee called the violence in Gujarat a reason for the BJP's electoral defeat and said it had been a mistake to leave Modi in office after the riots.<sup id="cite_ref-TellisWills_169-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TellisWills-169">&#91;158&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-170" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-170">&#91;159&#93;</a></sup> Western nations also raised questions about Modi's relationship with Muslims; the US <a href="/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State" title="United States Department of State">State Department</a> barred him from entering the United States in accordance with the recommendations of that country's <a href="/wiki/United_States_Commission_on_International_Religious_Freedom" title="United States Commission on International Religious Freedom">Commission on International Religious Freedom</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-2005_ban_171-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2005_ban-171">&#91;160&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-visa_denied_172-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-visa_denied-172">&#91;161&#93;</a></sup> the only person to be <a href="/wiki/List_of_people_barred_or_excluded_from_the_United_States" class="mw-redirect" title="List of people barred or excluded from the United States">denied a US visa</a> under this law.<sup id="cite_ref-2005_ban_171-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2005_ban-171">&#91;160&#93;</a></sup> The UK and the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a> (EU) refused to admit Modi because of what they saw as his role in the riots. As Modi rose to prominence in India, the UK<sup id="cite_ref-173" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-173">&#91;162&#93;</a></sup> and the EU<sup id="cite_ref-174" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-174">&#91;163&#93;</a></sup> lifted their bans in October 2012 and March 2013, respectively, and after his election as prime minister in 2014, the US lifted its ban and invited him to Washington, D.C.<sup id="cite_ref-175" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-175">&#91;164&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-newyorker-may14_176-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-newyorker-may14-176">&#91;165&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:The_Chief_Minister_of_Gujarat_Shri_Narendra_Modi_calls_on_the_Prime_Minister_Dr._Manmohan_Singh_in_New_Delhi_on_June_30,_2004.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/The_Chief_Minister_of_Gujarat_Shri_Narendra_Modi_calls_on_the_Prime_Minister_Dr._Manmohan_Singh_in_New_Delhi_on_June_30%2C_2004.jpg/220px-The_Chief_Minister_of_Gujarat_Shri_Narendra_Modi_calls_on_the_Prime_Minister_Dr._Manmohan_Singh_in_New_Delhi_on_June_30%2C_2004.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="175" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/The_Chief_Minister_of_Gujarat_Shri_Narendra_Modi_calls_on_the_Prime_Minister_Dr._Manmohan_Singh_in_New_Delhi_on_June_30%2C_2004.jpg/330px-The_Chief_Minister_of_Gujarat_Shri_Narendra_Modi_calls_on_the_Prime_Minister_Dr._Manmohan_Singh_in_New_Delhi_on_June_30%2C_2004.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a6/The_Chief_Minister_of_Gujarat_Shri_Narendra_Modi_calls_on_the_Prime_Minister_Dr._Manmohan_Singh_in_New_Delhi_on_June_30%2C_2004.jpg/440px-The_Chief_Minister_of_Gujarat_Shri_Narendra_Modi_calls_on_the_Prime_Minister_Dr._Manmohan_Singh_in_New_Delhi_on_June_30%2C_2004.jpg 2x" data-file-width="900" data-file-height="717" /></a><figcaption>Modi meeting with then-<a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_India" title="Prime Minister of India">Prime Minister of India</a> <a href="/wiki/Manmohan_Singh" title="Manmohan Singh">Manmohan Singh</a> in 2004</figcaption></figure>
<p>During the run-up to the <a href="/wiki/2007_Gujarat_Legislative_Assembly_election" title="2007 Gujarat Legislative Assembly election">2007 Gujarat Legislative Assembly election</a> and the <a href="/wiki/2009_Indian_general_election" title="2009 Indian general election">2009 Indian general election</a>, the BJP intensified its rhetoric on terrorism.<sup id="cite_ref-177" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-177">&#91;166&#93;</a></sup> Modi criticised Prime Minister <a href="/wiki/Manmohan_Singh" title="Manmohan Singh">Manmohan Singh</a> "for his reluctance to revive anti-terror legislation" such as the 2002 <a href="/wiki/Prevention_of_Terrorism_Act,_2002" title="Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2002">Prevention of Terrorism Act</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Telegraph_India_178-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Telegraph_India-178">&#91;167&#93;</a></sup> In 2007, Modi wrote <i>Karmayog</i>, a 101-page booklet discussing manual scavenging. In it, he said scavenging is a "spiritual experience" for Valmiks, a sub-caste of <a href="/wiki/Dalit" title="Dalit">Dalits</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-179" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-179">&#91;168&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-180" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-180">&#91;169&#93;</a></sup> The book was not circulated at that time because of the <a href="/wiki/Model_Code_of_Conduct" title="Model Code of Conduct">election code of conduct</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-181" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-181">&#91;170&#93;</a></sup> After the November <a href="/wiki/2008_Mumbai_attacks" title="2008 Mumbai attacks">2008 Mumbai attacks</a>, the Gujarat government authorized the deployment of 30 high-speed boats for coastal surveillance.<sup id="cite_ref-182" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-182">&#91;171&#93;</a></sup> In July 2007, Modi completed 2,063 consecutive days as chief minister of Gujarat, making him the longest-serving holder of that post.<sup id="cite_ref-183" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-183">&#91;172&#93;</a></sup> The BJP won 122 of 182 state-assembly seats in that year's election.<sup id="cite_ref-184" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-184">&#91;173&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Despite the BJP's shift away from explicit Hindutva, Modi's campaigns in <a href="/wiki/2007_Gujarat_Legislative_Assembly_election" title="2007 Gujarat Legislative Assembly election">2007</a> and <a href="/wiki/2012_Gujarat_Legislative_Assembly_election" title="2012 Gujarat Legislative Assembly election">2012</a> Gujarat Legislative Assembly elections contained elements of Hindu nationalism. He attended only Hindu religious ceremonies and had prominent associations with Hindu religious leaders. During his 2012 campaign, Modi twice refused to wear articles of clothing gifted by Muslim leaders.<sup id="cite_ref-India_Review_159-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-India_Review-159">&#91;148&#93;</a></sup> He did, however, maintain relations with <a href="/wiki/Dawoodi_Bohra" title="Dawoodi Bohra">Dawoodi Bohra</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-India_Review_159-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-India_Review-159">&#91;148&#93;</a></sup> Modi's 2012 campaign included references to issues known to cause religious polarisation, including <a href="/wiki/Afzal_Guru" title="Afzal Guru">Afzal Guru</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Death_of_Sohrabuddin_Sheikh" title="Death of Sohrabuddin Sheikh">death of Sohrabuddin Sheikh</a>. The BJP did not nominate any Muslim candidates for the 2012 assembly election.<sup id="cite_ref-India_Review_159-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-India_Review-159">&#91;148&#93;</a></sup> During the 2012 campaign, Modi attempted to identify himself with the state of Gujarat, a strategy similar to that used by Indira Gandhi during the Emergency, and projected himself as protecting Gujarat against persecution by the rest of India.<sup id="cite_ref-India_Review_159-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-India_Review-159">&#91;148&#93;</a></sup> While campaigning for the 2012 Gujarat Legislative Assembly election, Modi made extensive use of holograms and other technologies, allowing him to reach a large number of people,<sup id="cite_ref-Jaffrelot_T&amp;NM_157-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jaffrelot_T&amp;NM-157">&#91;146&#93;</a></sup> something he repeated in the 2014 general election. Modi won the constituency of Maninagar, defeating Shweta Bhatt of the INC.<sup id="cite_ref-big_win_185-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-big_win-185">&#91;174&#93;</a></sup> The BJP won 115 of the 182 seats, continuing its majority during his tenure.<sup id="cite_ref-186" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-186">&#91;175&#93;</a></sup> After his election as Prime Minister of India, Modi resigned as the Gujarat chief minister and as MLA for Maninagar. <a href="/wiki/Anandiben_Patel" title="Anandiben Patel">Anandiben Patel</a> succeeded Modi as chief minister.<sup id="cite_ref-187" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-187">&#91;176&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Development_projects">Development projects</span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Sardar_Sarovar_Dam_2006,_India.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Sardar_Sarovar_Dam_2006%2C_India.jpg/220px-Sardar_Sarovar_Dam_2006%2C_India.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Sardar_Sarovar_Dam_2006%2C_India.jpg/330px-Sardar_Sarovar_Dam_2006%2C_India.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/Sardar_Sarovar_Dam_2006%2C_India.jpg/440px-Sardar_Sarovar_Dam_2006%2C_India.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2048" data-file-height="1536" /></a><figcaption>The <a href="/wiki/Sardar_Sarovar_Dam" title="Sardar Sarovar Dam">Sardar Sarovar Dam</a> during a 2006 height increase</figcaption></figure>
<p>As chief minister, Modi favoured privatisation and <a href="/wiki/Small_government" class="mw-redirect" title="Small government">small government</a>, which was at odds with the philosophy of the RSS, which is usually described as anti-privatisation and anti-globalisation. Modi's policies during his second term have been credited with reducing corruption in Gujarat. He established financial and technology parks in the state and during the 2007 <a href="/wiki/Vibrant_Gujarat" title="Vibrant Gujarat">Vibrant Gujarat</a> summit, real-estate investment deals worth <span class="nowrap"><span style="white-space: nowrap">₹</span>6.6 trillion</span> (equivalent to <span style="white-space: nowrap">₹</span>20&#160;trillion&#32;or&#32;US$250&#160;billion in 2023) were signed.<sup id="cite_ref-Phadnis_BS_117-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Phadnis_BS-117">&#91;107&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The governments led by Patel and Modi supported NGOs and communities in the creation of groundwater-conservation projects. By December 2008, 500,000 structures had been built, of which 113,738 were <a href="/wiki/Check_dam" title="Check dam">check dams</a>, which helped recharge the aquifers beneath them.<sup id="cite_ref-Shah_BS_188-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Shah_BS-188">&#91;177&#93;</a></sup> Sixty of the 112 <a href="/wiki/Tehsil" title="Tehsil">tehsils</a> which had depleted the <a href="/wiki/Water_table" title="Water table">water table</a> in 2004 had regained their normal groundwater levels by 2010.<sup id="cite_ref-189" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-189">&#91;178&#93;</a></sup> As a result, the state's production of <a href="/wiki/Bt_cotton" title="Bt cotton">genetically modified cotton</a> increased to become the largest in India.<sup id="cite_ref-Shah_BS_188-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Shah_BS-188">&#91;177&#93;</a></sup> The boom in cotton production and its semi-arid land use<sup id="cite_ref-Farm_growth_Hindu_190-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Farm_growth_Hindu-190">&#91;179&#93;</a></sup> led to Gujarat's agricultural sector growing at an average rate of 9.6 percent from 2001 to 2007.<sup id="cite_ref-191" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-191">&#91;180&#93;</a></sup> Public irrigation measures in central and southern Gujarat, such as the <a href="/wiki/Sardar_Sarovar_Dam" title="Sardar Sarovar Dam">Sardar Sarovar Dam</a>, were less successful. The Sardar Sarovar project irrigated only 4–6% of the area intended.<sup id="cite_ref-Shah_BS_188-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Shah_BS-188">&#91;177&#93;</a></sup> In 2008, Modi offered land in Gujarat to <a href="/wiki/Tata_Motors" title="Tata Motors">Tata Motors</a> to set up a plant manufacturing the <a href="/wiki/Nano_(car)" class="mw-redirect" title="Nano (car)">Nano</a> car after popular agitation had forced the <a href="/wiki/Tata_Nano_Singur_controversy" title="Tata Nano Singur controversy">company to move out of West Bengal</a>. Following Tata, several other companies relocated to Gujarat.<sup id="cite_ref-Modi-nomics_192-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Modi-nomics-192">&#91;181&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The Modi government finished the process of taking electricity to every village in Gujarat its predecessor had almost completed.<sup id="cite_ref-Business_Standard_Vibrant_Gujarat_193-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Business_Standard_Vibrant_Gujarat-193">&#91;182&#93;</a></sup> Modi significantly changed the state's system of power distribution, greatly impacting farmers. Gujarat expanded the <a href="/wiki/Jyotigram_Yojana" title="Jyotigram Yojana">Jyotigram Yojana</a> scheme, in which agricultural electricity was separated from other rural electricity; the agricultural electricity was rationed to fit scheduled irrigation demands, reducing its cost. Early protests by farmers ended when those who benefitted found their electricity supply had stabilised<sup id="cite_ref-Shah_BS_188-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Shah_BS-188">&#91;177&#93;</a></sup> but, according to an assessment study, corporations and large farmers benefited from the policy at the expense of small farmers and labourers.<sup id="cite_ref-Shah_2008_194-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Shah_2008-194">&#91;183&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Development_debate">Development debate</span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Modi_at_GNLU.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Modi speaking at flower-decked podium" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/Modi_at_GNLU.jpg/180px-Modi_at_GNLU.jpg" decoding="async" width="180" height="272" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/Modi_at_GNLU.jpg/270px-Modi_at_GNLU.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f7/Modi_at_GNLU.jpg/360px-Modi_at_GNLU.jpg 2x" data-file-width="636" data-file-height="960" /></a><figcaption>Modi addressing graduates of the <a href="/wiki/Gujarat_National_Law_University" title="Gujarat National Law University">Gujarat National Law University</a> in 2012</figcaption></figure>
<p>A contentious debate surrounds the assessment of Gujarat's economic development during Modi's tenure as chief minister.<sup id="cite_ref-Basu_2014_195-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Basu_2014-195">&#91;184&#93;</a></sup> The state's <a href="/wiki/Gross_Domestic_Product" class="mw-redirect" title="Gross Domestic Product">Gross Domestic Product</a> (GDP) growth rate averaged 10% during his tenure, a rate similar to those of other highly industrialised states, and above that of India as a whole.<sup id="cite_ref-Modi-nomics_192-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Modi-nomics-192">&#91;181&#93;</a></sup> Gujarat also had a high rate of economic growth in the 1990s, before Modi took office; some scholars have stated growth did not much accelerate during his tenure.<sup id="cite_ref-Ghatak_196-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ghatak-196">&#91;185&#93;</a></sup> Under Modi, Gujarat topped the <a href="/wiki/World_Bank" title="World Bank">World Bank</a>'s "ease of doing business" rankings among Indian states for two consecutive years.<sup id="cite_ref-197" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-197">&#91;186&#93;</a></sup> In 2013, a report measuring governance, growth, citizens' rights, and labour and business regulation among the country's 20 largest states, ranked Gujarat first among Indian states for "economic freedom".<sup id="cite_ref-Modi-nomics_192-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Modi-nomics-192">&#91;181&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-198" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-198">&#91;187&#93;</a></sup> In the later years of Modi's government, Gujarat's economic growth was frequently used as an argument to counter allegations of communalism.<sup id="cite_ref-Bobbio_8-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bobbio-8">&#91;5&#93;</a></sup> Tax breaks and land for businesses were easier to obtain in Gujarat than in other states. Modi's policies of making Gujarat attractive for investment included the creation of <a href="/wiki/Special_Economic_Zones" class="mw-redirect" title="Special Economic Zones">Special Economic Zones</a> in which labour laws were greatly weakened.<sup id="cite_ref-India_Review_159-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-India_Review-159">&#91;148&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Despite its growth rate, Gujarat had a relatively poor record on human development, poverty relief, nutrition and education during Modi's tenure. In 2013, Gujarat ranked 13th in India with respect to rates of poverty, and 21st in education. Nearly 45 percent of children under five were underweight and 23 percent were undernourished, putting the state in the "alarming" category on the <a href="/wiki/India_State_Hunger_Index" class="mw-redirect" title="India State Hunger Index">India State Hunger Index</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-199" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-199">&#91;188&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Hariss_2015_200-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Hariss_2015-200">&#91;189&#93;</a></sup> A study by <a href="/wiki/UNICEF" title="UNICEF">UNICEF</a> and the Indian government found Gujarat under Modi had a poor record in <a href="/wiki/Immunisation" class="mw-redirect" title="Immunisation">immunisation</a> of children.<sup id="cite_ref-Economist_2015_201-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Economist_2015-201">&#91;190&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>From 2001 to 2011, Gujarat did not change its position relative to the rest of the country with respect to poverty and female literacy, remaining near the median of the 29 Indian states.<sup id="cite_ref-Gujarat_Model_140-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Gujarat_Model-140">&#91;129&#93;</a></sup> It showed a marginal improvement in rates of infant mortality and its position with respect to individual consumption declined.<sup id="cite_ref-Gujarat_Model_140-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Gujarat_Model-140">&#91;129&#93;</a></sup> The quality of education in government schools in Gujarat ranked below that of many Indian states.<sup id="cite_ref-Gujarat_Model_140-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Gujarat_Model-140">&#91;129&#93;</a></sup> The state government's social policies generally did not benefit Muslims, <a href="/wiki/Dalit" title="Dalit">Dalits</a> and <a href="/wiki/Adivasi" title="Adivasi">Adivasis</a>, and generally increased social inequalities.<sup id="cite_ref-Gujarat_Model_140-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Gujarat_Model-140">&#91;129&#93;</a></sup> Development in Gujarat was generally limited to the urban middle class, and citizens in rural areas and those from lower castes were increasingly marginalised. In 2013, the state ranked 10th of 21 Indian states in the <a href="/wiki/Human_Development_Index" title="Human Development Index">Human Development Index</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Jaffrelot2013_12-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jaffrelot2013-12">&#91;9&#93;</a></sup> Under Modi, the state government spent less than the national average on education and healthcare.<sup id="cite_ref-Gujarat_Model_140-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Gujarat_Model-140">&#91;129&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Allegations_of_bribery">Allegations of bribery</span></h3>
<p>During its raids in 2013 and 2014, the <a href="/wiki/Central_Bureau_of_Investigation" title="Central Bureau of Investigation">CBI</a> seized some diaries from two big Indian companies, <a href="/wiki/Sahara_Group" class="mw-redirect" title="Sahara Group">Sahara Group</a> and <a href="/wiki/Aditya_Birla_Group" title="Aditya Birla Group">Aditya Birla Group</a>. These diaries contained references of alleged payments leaders belonging to as many as 18 political parties including BJP, Congress, JDU, BJD etc.<sup id="cite_ref-diary_202-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-diary-202">&#91;191&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-laundry_203-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-laundry-203">&#91;192&#93;</a></sup> Among these were some entries mentioning "Gujarat CM"  and "Ahmadabad Modiji".<sup id="cite_ref-epw_204-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-epw-204">&#91;193&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-epw2_205-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-epw2-205">&#91;194&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-laundry_203-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-laundry-203">&#91;192&#93;</a></sup> Citing these entries, on 21 December 2016, the opposition leader Rahul Gandhi alleged that Modi received cash bribes worth ₹65 crore  from Sahara Group and Aditya Birla Group when he was the Chief Minister of Gujarat.<sup id="cite_ref-rahbr_206-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rahbr-206">&#91;195&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-207" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-207">&#91;196&#93;</a></sup> In November 2016, advocate <a href="/wiki/Prashant_Bhushan" title="Prashant Bhushan">Prashant Bhushan</a> had filed a plea in the <a href="/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_India" title="Supreme Court of India">Supreme Court of India</a> asking for investigation of the alleged bribe payments made to some senior public servants including Modi.<sup id="cite_ref-208" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-208">&#91;197&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-209" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-209">&#91;198&#93;</a></sup> A Supreme Court bench headed by Justice <a href="/wiki/Arun_Kumar_Mishra" title="Arun Kumar Mishra">Arun Kumar Mishra</a> dismissed the plea in January 2017 stating that the evidence provided was insufficient.<sup id="cite_ref-dis_210-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-dis-210">&#91;199&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-211" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-211">&#91;200&#93;</a></sup> Later on, Justice Mishra was criticised by a section of advocates and activists for siding with the Modi government in multiple judgements during his tenure at the Supreme Court.<sup id="cite_ref-212" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-212">&#91;201&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-213" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-213">&#91;202&#93;</a></sup> <i><a href="/wiki/The_Wire_(India)" title="The Wire (India)">The Wire</a></i> questioned the manner in which the Supreme Court buried the Sahara-Birla diaries' investigation.<sup id="cite_ref-214" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-214">&#91;203&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Premiership_campaigns">Premiership campaigns</span></h2>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="2014_Indian_general_election">2014 Indian general election</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party_campaign_for_the_2014_Indian_general_election" title="Bharatiya Janata Party campaign for the 2014 Indian general election">Bharatiya Janata Party campaign for the 2014 Indian general election</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Narendra_Modi_hands_over_his_resignation_as_Maninagar_MLA_to_the_Speaker_of_the_Gujarat_Vidhan_Sabha.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Narendra_Modi_hands_over_his_resignation_as_Maninagar_MLA_to_the_Speaker_of_the_Gujarat_Vidhan_Sabha.jpg/220px-Narendra_Modi_hands_over_his_resignation_as_Maninagar_MLA_to_the_Speaker_of_the_Gujarat_Vidhan_Sabha.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Narendra_Modi_hands_over_his_resignation_as_Maninagar_MLA_to_the_Speaker_of_the_Gujarat_Vidhan_Sabha.jpg/330px-Narendra_Modi_hands_over_his_resignation_as_Maninagar_MLA_to_the_Speaker_of_the_Gujarat_Vidhan_Sabha.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/11/Narendra_Modi_hands_over_his_resignation_as_Maninagar_MLA_to_the_Speaker_of_the_Gujarat_Vidhan_Sabha.jpg 2x" data-file-width="400" data-file-height="267" /></a><figcaption>Narendra Modi hands over his resignation as <a href="/wiki/Maninagar_(Vidhan_Sabha_constituency)" class="mw-redirect" title="Maninagar (Vidhan Sabha constituency)">Maninagar</a> MLA to the Speaker of the <a href="/wiki/Gujarat_Vidhan_Sabha" class="mw-redirect" title="Gujarat Vidhan Sabha">Gujarat Vidhan Sabha</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1066479718"><table class="infobox" style="float: right; clear: right; margin:0 0 1.5em 1.5em"><tbody><tr><th colspan="2" class="infobox-above" style="font-size:115%">External video</th></tr><tr><td colspan="2" class="infobox-full-data" style="text-align: left"><span typeof="mw:File"><span><img alt="video icon" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/16px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png" decoding="async" width="16" height="16" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/24px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/32px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="128" data-file-height="128" /></span></span> <a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wgeKLJuJMp8">BJP announces Shri Narendra Modi as its Prime Ministerial candidate for Loksabha Elections.</a> Bharatiya Janata Party on <a href="/wiki/YouTube" title="YouTube">YouTube</a>, 13 September 2013</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>In September 2013, Modi was named the BJP's candidate for prime minister ahead of the <a href="/wiki/2014_Lok_Sabha_election" class="mw-redirect" title="2014 Lok Sabha election">2014 Lok Sabha election</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Chhibber_215-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Chhibber-215">&#91;204&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-216" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-216">&#91;205&#93;</a></sup> Several BJP leaders,<sup id="cite_ref-Jaffrelot_2015_217-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jaffrelot_2015-217">&#91;206&#93;</a></sup> including BJP founding member L. K.
