Advani who cited concern with leaders who were "concerned with their personal agendas", expressed opposition to Modi's candidature.<sup id="cite_ref-218" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-218">&#91;207&#93;</a></sup> Modi played a dominant role in the BJP's 2009 general election campaign.<sup id="cite_ref-219" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-219">&#91;208&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-T&amp;NM_2015_220-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-T&amp;NM_2015-220">&#91;209&#93;</a></sup> Several people who voted for the BJP stated they would have voted for another party if Modi had not been the prime-ministerial candidate.<sup id="cite_ref-Chhibber_215-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Chhibber-215">&#91;204&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Chacko_221-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Chacko-221">&#91;210&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Srivastava_222-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Srivastava-222">&#91;211&#93;</a></sup> The focus on Modi as an individual was unusual for a BJP election campaign.<sup id="cite_ref-Jaffrelot_2015_217-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jaffrelot_2015-217">&#91;206&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-223" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-223">&#91;212&#93;</a></sup> The election was described as a referendum on Narendra Modi.<sup id="cite_ref-Basu_2014_195-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Basu_2014-195">&#91;184&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Narendra_Modi_meets_his_mother_after_winning_the_2014_elections.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/Narendra_Modi_meets_his_mother_after_winning_the_2014_elections.jpg/220px-Narendra_Modi_meets_his_mother_after_winning_the_2014_elections.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/Narendra_Modi_meets_his_mother_after_winning_the_2014_elections.jpg/330px-Narendra_Modi_meets_his_mother_after_winning_the_2014_elections.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/Narendra_Modi_meets_his_mother_after_winning_the_2014_elections.jpg/440px-Narendra_Modi_meets_his_mother_after_winning_the_2014_elections.jpg 2x" data-file-width="690" data-file-height="458" /></a><figcaption>Modi meets his mother after winning the <a href="/wiki/2014_Indian_general_election" title="2014 Indian general election">2014 Indian general election</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>During the campaign, Modi focused on corruption scandals under the previous Congress government, and played on his image as a politician who had created a high rate of GDP growth in Gujarat.<sup id="cite_ref-Jaffrelot_2015_217-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jaffrelot_2015-217">&#91;206&#93;</a></sup> He projected himself as a person who could bring about "development" without focusing on specific policies.<sup id="cite_ref-Jaffrelot_2015_217-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jaffrelot_2015-217">&#91;206&#93;</a></sup> His message found support among young and middle-class people. The BJP under Modi was able to downplay concerns about the protection of religious minorities and Modi's commitment to secularism, areas in which he had previously received criticism.<sup id="cite_ref-T&amp;NM_2015_220-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-T&amp;NM_2015-220">&#91;209&#93;</a></sup> Prior to the election, Modi's media image had centred around his role in the 2002 Gujarat riots but during the campaign, the BJP focused on Modi's <a href="/wiki/Neoliberalism" title="Neoliberalism">neoliberal</a> ideology and the Gujarat model of development.<sup id="cite_ref-T&amp;NM_2015_220-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-T&amp;NM_2015-220">&#91;209&#93;</a></sup> The BJP sought to identify itself with political leaders who publicly opposed <a href="/wiki/Hindu_nationalism" title="Hindu nationalism">Hindu nationalism</a>, including <a href="/wiki/B._R._Ambedkar" title="B. R. Ambedkar">B. R. Ambedkar</a>, <a href="/wiki/Subhas_Chandra_Bose" title="Subhas Chandra Bose">Subhas Chandra Bose</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ram_Manohar_Lohia" title="Ram Manohar Lohia">Ram Manohar Lohia</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Manor_168-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Manor-168">&#91;157&#93;</a></sup> Hindutva remained a part of the campaign; BJP leaders used Hindutva-based rhetoric in several states.<sup id="cite_ref-Palshikar_224-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Palshikar-224">&#91;213&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Jaffrelot_2015_217-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jaffrelot_2015-217">&#91;206&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Chacko_221-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Chacko-221">&#91;210&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Ganguly_2014_45-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ganguly_2014-45">&#91;38&#93;</a></sup> Communal tensions were played upon, especially in Uttar Pradesh and <a href="/wiki/Northeast_India" title="Northeast India">Northeast India</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Palshikar_224-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Palshikar-224">&#91;213&#93;</a></sup> A proposal for the controversial <a href="/wiki/Uniform_Civil_Code" title="Uniform Civil Code">Uniform Civil Code</a> was a part of the BJP's election manifesto.<sup id="cite_ref-Ganguly_2014_45-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ganguly_2014-45">&#91;38&#93;</a></sup>
The BJP's campaign was assisted by its wide influence in the media.<sup id="cite_ref-Hariss_2015_200-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Hariss_2015-200">&#91;189&#93;</a></sup> Modi's campaign blitz cost around <span class="nowrap"><span style="white-space: nowrap">₹</span>50 billion</span> (US$630&#160;million)<sup id="cite_ref-Basu_2014_195-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Basu_2014-195">&#91;184&#93;</a></sup> and the BJP received extensive financial support from corporate donors.<sup id="cite_ref-225" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-225">&#91;214&#93;</a></sup> In addition to more-conventional campaign methods, Modi made extensive use of social media<sup id="cite_ref-Basu_2014_195-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Basu_2014-195">&#91;184&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Jaffrelot_2015_217-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jaffrelot_2015-217">&#91;206&#93;</a></sup> and addressed more than 1,000 rallies via hologram appearances.<sup id="cite_ref-Ganguly_2014_45-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ganguly_2014-45">&#91;38&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The BJP won 31 percent of the vote,<sup id="cite_ref-Stepan_44-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Stepan-44">&#91;37&#93;</a></sup> and more-than-doubled its number of seats in the Lok Sabha to 282, becoming the first party to win a majority of seats on its own since <a href="/wiki/1984_Indian_general_election" title="1984 Indian general election">1984</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-T&amp;NM_2015_220-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-T&amp;NM_2015-220">&#91;209&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Chacko_221-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Chacko-221">&#91;210&#93;</a></sup> Voter dissatisfaction with the Congress and with regional parties in North India, and support from the RSS were reasons for the BJP's success.<sup id="cite_ref-Chacko_221-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Chacko-221">&#91;210&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Jaffrelot_2015_217-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jaffrelot_2015-217">&#91;206&#93;</a></sup> In states such as Uttar Pradesh, where the BJP performed well, it drew exceptionally high support from upper-caste Hindus, and its Muslim vote increased to 10 percent. The BJP performed particularly well in parts of the country that had recently experienced violence between Hindus and Muslims.<sup id="cite_ref-Chacko_221-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Chacko-221">&#91;210&#93;</a></sup> The magnitude of the BJP's victory led many commentators to say the election constituted a political realignment away from <a href="/wiki/Progressivism" title="Progressivism">progressive parties</a> towards the right-wing.<sup id="cite_ref-Ganguly_2014_45-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ganguly_2014-45">&#91;38&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Basu_2014_195-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Basu_2014-195">&#91;184&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Chacko_221-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Chacko-221">&#91;210&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-226" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-226">&#91;215&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-227" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-227">&#91;216&#93;</a></sup> Modi's tweet announcing his victory was described as being emblematic of the political realignment away from a secular, socialist state towards capitalism and Hindu cultural nationalism.<sup id="cite_ref-Kaur_2015_228-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Kaur_2015-228">&#91;217&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Modi was a candidate for the Lok Sabha constituencies <a href="/wiki/Varanasi_Lok_Sabha_constituency" title="Varanasi Lok Sabha constituency">Varanasi</a> and <a href="/wiki/Vadodara_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)" class="mw-redirect" title="Vadodara (Lok Sabha constituency)">Vadodara</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-grand_roadshow_229-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-grand_roadshow-229">&#91;218&#93;</a></sup> He won in both constituencies, defeating <a href="/wiki/Aam_Aadmi_Party" title="Aam Aadmi Party">Aam Aadmi Party</a> leader <a href="/wiki/Arvind_Kejriwal" title="Arvind Kejriwal">Arvind Kejriwal</a> in Varanasi by 371,784 votes and <a href="/wiki/Madhusudan_Mistry" title="Madhusudan Mistry">Madhusudan Mistry</a> of the Congress in Vadodara by 570,128 votes.<sup id="cite_ref-230" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-230">&#91;219&#93;</a></sup> India's president appointed Modi, who was unanimously elected leader of the BJP, Prime Minister of India.<sup id="cite_ref-appointment-prez_231-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-appointment-prez-231">&#91;220&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-appointment-IE_232-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-appointment-IE-232">&#91;221&#93;</a></sup> To comply with the law prohibiting MPs from representing more than one constituency, he vacated the Vadodara seat.<sup id="cite_ref-233" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-233">&#91;222&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="2019_Indian_general_election">2019 Indian general election</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party_campaign_for_the_2019_Indian_general_election" title="Bharatiya Janata Party campaign for the 2019 Indian general election">Bharatiya Janata Party campaign for the 2019 Indian general election</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1066479718"><table class="infobox" style="float: right; clear: right; margin:0 0 1.5em 1.5em"><tbody><tr><th colspan="2" class="infobox-above" style="font-size:115%">External video</th></tr><tr><td colspan="2" class="infobox-full-data" style="text-align: left"><span typeof="mw:File"><span><img alt="video icon" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/16px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png" decoding="async" width="16" height="16" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/24px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/32px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="128" data-file-height="128" /></span></span> <a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QoORekBf6pE">BJP announced manifesto and Shri Narendra Modi as prime minister candidate.</a> Bharatiya Janata Party on <a href="/wiki/YouTube" title="YouTube">YouTube</a>, 8 April 2019.</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>On 13 October 2018, Modi was named the BJP candidate for prime minister in the <a href="/wiki/2019_Indian_general_election" title="2019 Indian general election">2019 general election</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-234" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-234">&#91;223&#93;</a></sup> The BJP's chief campaigner was its president <a href="/wiki/Amit_Shah" title="Amit Shah">Amit Shah</a>. Modi launched the party's <i><a href="/wiki/Main_Bhi_Chowkidar" title="Main Bhi Chowkidar">Main Bhi Chowkidar</a></i> ("I too am a watchman") campaign ahead of the general election, against the INC's campaign slogan <i><a href="/wiki/Chowkidar_Chor_Hai" title="Chowkidar Chor Hai">Chowkidar Chor Hai</a></i> ("The watchman is a thief").<sup id="cite_ref-235" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-235">&#91;224&#93;</a></sup> In 2018, the <a href="/wiki/Telugu_Desam_Party" title="Telugu Desam Party">Telugu Desam Party</a> split from the NDA over the campaign for special status for <a href="/wiki/Andhra_Pradesh" title="Andhra Pradesh">Andhra Pradesh</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-236" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-236">&#91;225&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Amit_Shah" title="Amit Shah">Amit Shah</a> launched the BJP's election campaign on 8 April 2019. In the campaign, the opposition targeted Modi on allegations of corruption over the <a href="/wiki/Rafale_deal" class="mw-redirect" title="Rafale deal">Rafale deal</a> with the <a href="/wiki/Government_of_France" title="Government of France">Government of France</a>, highlighting the <a href="/wiki/Rafale_deal_controversy" title="Rafale deal controversy">controversy surrounding the deal</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-237" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-237">&#91;226&#93;</a></sup> Modi's campaign focused on defence and national security, especially after the <a href="/wiki/2019_Pulwama_attack" title="2019 Pulwama attack">Pulwama attack</a> and the retaliatory <a href="/wiki/2019_Balakot_airstrike" title="2019 Balakot airstrike">Balakot airstrike</a>, which was counted as an achievement of his administration.<sup id="cite_ref-BS_Book_review_22-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-BS_Book_review-22">&#91;16&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-238" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-238">&#91;227&#93;</a></sup> Other topics in the campaign were development and <a href="/wiki/Foreign_policy_of_the_Narendra_Modi_government" title="Foreign policy of the Narendra Modi government">good foreign relations</a> in the first premiership.<sup id="cite_ref-239" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-239">&#91;228&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Modi contested the Lok Sabha election as a candidate for <a href="/wiki/Varanasi_(Lok_Sabha_constituency)" class="mw-redirect" title="Varanasi (Lok Sabha constituency)">Varanasi</a>; he won the seat by a margin of 479,505 votes, defeating Shalini Yadav of the <a href="/wiki/Samajwadi_Party" title="Samajwadi Party">Samajwadi Party</a> (SP), who stood as a candidate for the SP-<a href="/wiki/Bahujan_Samaj_Party" title="Bahujan Samaj Party">BSP</a> alliance.<sup id="cite_ref-240" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-240">&#91;229&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-241" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-241">&#91;230&#93;</a></sup> Modi was unanimously appointed prime minister for a second time by the <a href="/wiki/National_Democratic_Alliance" title="National Democratic Alliance">National Democratic Alliance</a><sup id="cite_ref-242" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-242">&#91;231&#93;</a></sup> after the alliance won the election for the second time with 353 seats in the Lok Sabha; the BJP alone won 303 seats.<sup id="cite_ref-243" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-243">&#91;232&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-244" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-244">&#91;233&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Prime_Minister">Prime Minister</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Premiership_of_Narendra_Modi" title="Premiership of Narendra Modi">Premiership of Narendra Modi</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">For a chronological guide, see <a href="/wiki/Timeline_of_the_premiership_of_Narendra_Modi" title="Timeline of the premiership of Narendra Modi">Timeline of the premiership of Narendra Modi</a>.</div><figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Shri_Narendra_Modi_sworn_in_as_Prime_Minister.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Shri_Narendra_Modi_sworn_in_as_Prime_Minister.jpg/220px-Shri_Narendra_Modi_sworn_in_as_Prime_Minister.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="149" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Shri_Narendra_Modi_sworn_in_as_Prime_Minister.jpg/330px-Shri_Narendra_Modi_sworn_in_as_Prime_Minister.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/Shri_Narendra_Modi_sworn_in_as_Prime_Minister.jpg/440px-Shri_Narendra_Modi_sworn_in_as_Prime_Minister.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2000" data-file-height="1352" /></a><figcaption>Modi taking the oath of office as the <a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_India" title="Prime Minister of India">Prime Minister of India</a>, with President <a href="/wiki/Pranab_Mukherjee" title="Pranab Mukherjee">Pranab Mukherjee</a> administering the oath</figcaption></figure>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:The_President,_Shri_Ram_Nath_Kovind_administering_the_oath_of_office_of_the_Prime_Minister_to_Shri_Narendra_Modi,_at_a_Swearing-in_Ceremony,_at_Rashtrapati_Bhavan,_in_New_Delhi_on_May_30,_2019_(3).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/The_President%2C_Shri_Ram_Nath_Kovind_administering_the_oath_of_office_of_the_Prime_Minister_to_Shri_Narendra_Modi%2C_at_a_Swearing-in_Ceremony%2C_at_Rashtrapati_Bhavan%2C_in_New_Delhi_on_May_30%2C_2019_%283%29.jpg/220px-thumbnail.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="125" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/The_President%2C_Shri_Ram_Nath_Kovind_administering_the_oath_of_office_of_the_Prime_Minister_to_Shri_Narendra_Modi%2C_at_a_Swearing-in_Ceremony%2C_at_Rashtrapati_Bhavan%2C_in_New_Delhi_on_May_30%2C_2019_%283%29.jpg/330px-thumbnail.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/The_President%2C_Shri_Ram_Nath_Kovind_administering_the_oath_of_office_of_the_Prime_Minister_to_Shri_Narendra_Modi%2C_at_a_Swearing-in_Ceremony%2C_at_Rashtrapati_Bhavan%2C_in_New_Delhi_on_May_30%2C_2019_%283%29.jpg/440px-thumbnail.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2200" data-file-height="1251" /></a><figcaption>Modi taking the oath of office as the <a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_India" title="Prime Minister of India">Prime Minister of India</a> for the <a href="/wiki/Second_swearing-in_ceremony_of_Narendra_Modi" title="Second swearing-in ceremony of Narendra Modi">second time</a>, with President <a href="/wiki/Ram_Nath_Kovind" title="Ram Nath Kovind">Ram Nath Kovind</a> administering the oath</figcaption></figure>
<p>After the <a href="/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party" title="Bharatiya Janata Party">Bharatiya Janata Party</a>-led <a href="/wiki/National_Democratic_Alliance" title="National Democratic Alliance">National Democratic Alliance</a> (NDA) won a landslide in the <a href="/wiki/2014_Indian_general_election" title="2014 Indian general election">2014 Lok Sabha election</a>, Modi was <a href="/wiki/First_swearing-in_ceremony_of_Narendra_Modi" title="First swearing-in ceremony of Narendra Modi">sworn in as Prime Minister (PM) of India</a> on 26 May 2014, becoming the first Indian PM to be born after <a href="/wiki/Indian_Independence_Act_1947" title="Indian Independence Act 1947">the country's independence</a> from the <a href="/wiki/British_Empire" title="British Empire">British Empire</a> in 1947.<sup id="cite_ref-TOI-20140520_245-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-TOI-20140520-245">&#91;234&#93;</a></sup> Modi's second term as PM began in 2019 following the NDA's <a href="/wiki/2019_Indian_general_election" title="2019 Indian general election">2019 Lok Sabha election win</a>. On 6 December 2020, he became the fourth-longest-serving Prime Minister of India and the longest-serving non-<a href="/wiki/Indian_National_Congress" title="Indian National Congress">Congress</a> prime minister.<sup id="cite_ref-246" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-246">&#91;235&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Governance_and_other_initiatives">Governance and other initiatives</span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:The_Prime_Minister,_Shri_Narendra_Modi_walking_towards_the_dais_to_address_the_Nation_at_Red_Fort,_on_the_occasion_of_75th_Independence_Day,_in_Delhi_on_August_15,_2021_(2).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_walking_towards_the_dais_to_address_the_Nation_at_Red_Fort%2C_on_the_occasion_of_75th_Independence_Day%2C_in_Delhi_on_August_15%2C_2021_%282%29.jpg/220px-thumbnail.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="158" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_walking_towards_the_dais_to_address_the_Nation_at_Red_Fort%2C_on_the_occasion_of_75th_Independence_Day%2C_in_Delhi_on_August_15%2C_2021_%282%29.jpg/330px-thumbnail.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_walking_towards_the_dais_to_address_the_Nation_at_Red_Fort%2C_on_the_occasion_of_75th_Independence_Day%2C_in_Delhi_on_August_15%2C_2021_%282%29.jpg/440px-thumbnail.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2200" data-file-height="1583" /></a><figcaption>Prime Minister Modi walking towards the dais to address the Nation at <a href="/wiki/Red_Fort" title="Red Fort">Red Fort</a>, on the occasion of <a href="/wiki/75th_Anniversary_of_Indian_Independence" title="75th Anniversary of Indian Independence">75th Independence Day</a>, in Delhi on 15 August 2021</figcaption></figure>
<p>Modi's first year as PM saw significant centralisation of power.<sup id="cite_ref-Manor_168-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Manor-168">&#91;157&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Wyatt_247-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Wyatt-247">&#91;236&#93;</a></sup> Modi, who initially lacked a majority in the <a href="/wiki/Rajya_Sabha" title="Rajya Sabha">Rajya Sabha</a>, the upper house of Indian Parliament, passed a number of ordinances to enact his policies, leading to further centralisation of power.<sup id="cite_ref-Ronojoy_248-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ronojoy-248">&#91;237&#93;</a></sup> His administration enacted a bill to increase its control over the appointment of judges and reducing that of the <a href="/wiki/Judiciary_of_India" title="Judiciary of India">judiciary</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Stepan_44-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Stepan-44">&#91;37&#93;</a></sup> In December 2014, he abolished the <a href="/wiki/Planning_Commission_(India)" title="Planning Commission (India)">Planning Commission</a>, replacing it with the <a href="/wiki/NITI_Aayog" title="NITI Aayog">National Institution for Transforming India</a> (NITI Aayog),<sup id="cite_ref-Reuters_2015_249-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Reuters_2015-249">&#91;238&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Sengupta_250-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Sengupta-250">&#91;239&#93;</a></sup> concentrating the power previously with the planning commission in the person of the PM.<sup id="cite_ref-Ronojoy_248-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ronojoy-248">&#91;237&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Reuters_2015_249-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Reuters_2015-249">&#91;238&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Sengupta_250-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Sengupta-250">&#91;239&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Ruparelia_251-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ruparelia-251">&#91;240&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Patnaik_252-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Patnaik-252">&#91;241&#93;</a></sup> The Planning Commission had in previous years been criticised for creating inefficiency in the government and of not fulfilling its role of improving social welfare but since the <a href="/wiki/Economic_liberalisation_in_India" title="Economic liberalisation in India">economic liberalisation of the 1990s</a>, it had been the major government body responsible for measures related to social justice.<sup id="cite_ref-Sengupta_250-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Sengupta-250">&#91;239&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In its first year of administration, the Modi government launched investigations through the <a href="/wiki/Intelligence_Bureau_(India)" title="Intelligence Bureau (India)">Intelligence Bureau</a> into numerous civil society organisations and foreign non-governmental organisations (NGOs) on the grounds these organisations were slowing economic growth. The investigations were criticised as a <a href="/wiki/Witch_hunt" class="mw-redirect" title="Witch hunt">witch hunt</a>. International humanitarian aid organisation <a href="/wiki/Medecins_Sans_Frontieres" class="mw-redirect" title="Medecins Sans Frontieres">Medecins Sans Frontieres</a>, and environmental nonprofit organisation <a href="/wiki/Sierra_Club" title="Sierra Club">Sierra Club</a> and <a href="/wiki/Avaaz" title="Avaaz">Avaaz</a> were among the groups that were investigated.<sup id="cite_ref-Manor_168-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Manor-168">&#91;157&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Ruparelia_251-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ruparelia-251">&#91;240&#93;</a></sup> Cases of sedition and terrorism laws were filed against individuals who criticised the government.<sup id="cite_ref-Manor_168-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Manor-168">&#91;157&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-theguardian-uapa_253-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-theguardian-uapa-253">&#91;242&#93;</a></sup> This led to discontent within the BJP about his style of functioning and drew comparisons to the governing style of Indira Gandhi.<sup id="cite_ref-Manor_168-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Manor-168">&#91;157&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Ronojoy_248-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ronojoy-248">&#91;237&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Modi repealed 1,200 obsolete laws in first three years as prime minister; 1,301 such laws had been repealed by previous governments in the previous 64 years.<sup id="cite_ref-254" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-254">&#91;243&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-255" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-255">&#91;244&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-256" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-256">&#91;245&#93;</a></sup> Modi launched the <a href="/wiki/Digital_India" title="Digital India">Digital India</a> programme with the goal of ensuring government services are available electronically, build infrastructure to provide high-speed Internet access to rural areas, boost manufacturing of electronic goods in the country, and promote <a href="/wiki/Digital_literacy" title="Digital literacy">digital literacy</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-257" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-257">&#91;246&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-258" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-258">&#91;247&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2019, a law to reserve 10 percent of educational admission and government jobs for economically disadvantaged individuals was passed.<sup id="cite_ref-259" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-259">&#91;248&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-260" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-260">&#91;249&#93;</a></sup> In 2016, Modi's administration launched the <a href="/wiki/Ujjwala_scheme" class="mw-redirect" title="Ujjwala scheme">Ujjwala scheme</a> to provide free <a href="/wiki/Liquefied_petroleum_gas" title="Liquefied petroleum gas">liquefied petroleum gas</a> (LPG) connections to rural households. The scheme led to an additional 24% of Indian households having access to LPG in 2019 as compared to 2014.<sup id="cite_ref-261" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-261">&#91;250&#93;</a></sup> In 2022, the government eliminated LPG subsidies for all citizens except those covered by the Ujjwala program.<sup id="cite_ref-262" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-262">&#91;251&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Since May 2023, ethnic tensions between some groups have resulted in <a href="/wiki/2023_Manipur_violence" title="2023 Manipur violence">violent clashes</a> in <a href="/wiki/Manipur" title="Manipur">Manipur</a>. After 1 month of the violence, nearly 100 were killed and more than 36,000 people were displaced.<sup id="cite_ref-Parashar_263-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Parashar-263">&#91;252&#93;</a></sup> Narendra Modi has been criticized for his lack of reaction towards the violence.<sup id="cite_ref-The_Federal_264-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-The_Federal-264">&#91;253&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Hindutva">Hindutva</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Hindutva" title="Hindutva">Hindutva</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:The_Prime_Minister,_Shri_Narendra_Modi_pays_obeisance_at_Tirumala_Temple,_in_Tirupati,_Andhra_Pradesh.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_pays_obeisance_at_Tirumala_Temple%2C_in_Tirupati%2C_Andhra_Pradesh.jpg/220px-The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_pays_obeisance_at_Tirumala_Temple%2C_in_Tirupati%2C_Andhra_Pradesh.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="131" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_pays_obeisance_at_Tirumala_Temple%2C_in_Tirupati%2C_Andhra_Pradesh.jpg/330px-The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_pays_obeisance_at_Tirumala_Temple%2C_in_Tirupati%2C_Andhra_Pradesh.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_pays_obeisance_at_Tirumala_Temple%2C_in_Tirupati%2C_Andhra_Pradesh.jpg/440px-The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_pays_obeisance_at_Tirumala_Temple%2C_in_Tirupati%2C_Andhra_Pradesh.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1530" data-file-height="912" /></a><figcaption>Modi pays obeisance at <a href="/wiki/Tirumala_Temple" class="mw-redirect" title="Tirumala Temple">Tirumala Temple</a> in Andhra Pradesh.</figcaption></figure>
<p>The activities of a number of Hindu nationalist organisations increased in scope after Modi's appointment as prime minister, sometimes with the government's support.<sup id="cite_ref-265" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-265">&#91;254&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-266" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-266">&#91;255&#93;</a></sup> These activities included a <a href="/wiki/Ghar_Wapsi" title="Ghar Wapsi">Hindu religious conversion programme</a>, a campaign against the supposed Islamic practice of "<a href="/wiki/Love_Jihad" class="mw-redirect" title="Love Jihad">Love Jihad</a>" and attempts to celebrate <a href="/wiki/Nathuram_Godse" title="Nathuram Godse">Nathuram Godse</a>, the assassin of <a href="/wiki/Mahatma_Gandhi" title="Mahatma Gandhi">Mahatma Gandhi</a>, by members of the right-wing organisation <a href="/wiki/Hindu_Mahasabha" title="Hindu Mahasabha">Hindu Mahasabha</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-267" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-267">&#91;256&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-268" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-268">&#91;257&#93;</a></sup> Government officials, including the Home Minister, defended the conversion programmes.<sup id="cite_ref-Palshikar_224-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Palshikar-224">&#91;213&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Links between the BJP and the <a href="/wiki/Rashtriya_Swayamsevak_Sangh" title="Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh">Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh</a> (RSS) grew stronger under Modi. The RSS provided organisational support to the BJP's electoral campaigns while the Modi administration appointed RSS-affiliated individuals to prominent government positions.<sup id="cite_ref-Orange_Evolution_269-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Orange_Evolution-269">&#91;258&#93;</a></sup> In 2014, <a href="/wiki/Yellapragada_Sudershan_Rao" title="Yellapragada Sudershan Rao">Yellapragada Sudershan Rao</a>, who had previously been associated with the RSS, became the chairperson of the <a href="/wiki/Indian_Council_of_Historical_Research" title="Indian Council of Historical Research">Indian Council of Historical Research</a> (ICHR).<sup id="cite_ref-Ganguly_2014_45-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ganguly_2014-45">&#91;38&#93;</a></sup> Historians and former members of the ICHR, including those sympathetic to the BJP, questioned Rao's credentials as a historian and stated the appointment was part of an agenda of cultural nationalism.<sup id="cite_ref-Ganguly_2014_45-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ganguly_2014-45">&#91;38&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-saffronisation_270-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-saffronisation-270">&#91;259&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-right_wing_271-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-right_wing-271">&#91;260&#93;</a></sup> During its first term, the Modi administration appointed other RSS members to lead universities and research institutions, and recruitment of faculty members favouring the RSS increased. According to scholars <a href="/wiki/Nandini_Sundar" title="Nandini Sundar">Nandini Sundar</a> and Kiran Bhatty, many of these appointees did not possess the qualifications for their positions.<sup id="cite_ref-Bhatty_Sundar_pp._632–650_272-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bhatty_Sundar_pp._632–650-272">&#91;261&#93;</a></sup> The Modi administration also made numerous changes in government-approved history textbooks that de-emphasised the role of <a href="/wiki/Jawaharlal_Nehru" title="Jawaharlal Nehru">Jawaharlal Nehru</a> and glorified that of Modi while also portraying Indian society as harmonious, and without conflict and inequity.<sup id="cite_ref-Bhatty_Sundar_pp._632–650_272-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bhatty_Sundar_pp._632–650-272">&#91;261&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Bhatty_2019_273-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bhatty_2019-273">&#91;262&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2019, the Modi administration passed a <a href="/wiki/Citizenship_(Amendment)_Act,_2019" title="Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019">citizenship law</a> that provides a route to Indian citizenship for persecuted religious minorities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan who are Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis or Christians,<sup id="cite_ref-BBC_explained_274-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-BBC_explained-274">&#91;263&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-PIBPassesBill_275-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-PIBPassesBill-275">&#91;264&#93;</a></sup> but does not grant eligibility to Muslims.<sup id="cite_ref-CNNExcludes_276-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CNNExcludes-276">&#91;265&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-NPRExcludes_277-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NPRExcludes-277">&#91;266&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Washington_Post_278-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Washington_Post-278">&#91;267&#93;</a></sup> This was first time religion had been overtly used as a criterion for citizenship under Indian law; it attracted global criticism and prompted widespread <a href="/wiki/Citizenship_Amendment_Act_protests" title="Citizenship Amendment Act protests">protests</a> that were halted by the <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_India" title="COVID-19 pandemic in India">COVID-19 pandemic</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Bhatty_Sundar_pp._632–650_272-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bhatty_Sundar_pp._632–650-272">&#91;261&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Washington_Post_278-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Washington_Post-278">&#91;267&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-279" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-279">&#91;268&#93;</a></sup> Counter-demonstrations against the protests developed into the <a href="/wiki/2020_Delhi_riots" title="2020 Delhi riots">2020 Delhi riots</a>, caused chiefly by Hindu mobs attacking Muslims.<sup id="cite_ref-280" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-280">&#91;269&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-281" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-281">&#91;270&#93;</a></sup> Fifty-three people were killed in the protests, two-thirds of whom were Muslim.<sup id="cite_ref-nytimes-2020-3-12-two-thirds_282-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-nytimes-2020-3-12-two-thirds-282">&#91;271&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-wapo-3-6-20-slater-1_283-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-wapo-3-6-20-slater-1-283">&#91;272&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-wapo-3-2-20-slater-1_284-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-wapo-3-2-20-slater-1-284">&#91;273&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-285" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-285">&#91;274&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-286" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-286">&#91;275&#93;</a></sup> On 5 August 2020, Modi visited <a href="/wiki/Ayodhya" title="Ayodhya">Ayodhya</a> after the <a href="/wiki/2019_Supreme_Court_verdict_on_Ayodhya_dispute" title="2019 Supreme Court verdict on Ayodhya dispute">Supreme Court in 2019</a> ordered <a href="/wiki/Ayodhya_dispute" title="Ayodhya dispute">contested land in Ayodhya</a> to be handed to a trust to build a Hindu temple and ordered the government to give alternative 5 acres (2.0&#160;ha) of land to the <a href="/wiki/Sunni_Waqf_Board" class="mw-redirect" title="Sunni Waqf Board">Sunni Waqf Board</a> for the purpose of building a mosque.<sup id="cite_ref-287" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-287">&#91;276&#93;</a></sup> Modi became the first PM to visit temples at <a href="/wiki/Ram_Janmabhoomi" title="Ram Janmabhoomi">Ram Janmabhoomi</a> and <a href="/wiki/Hanuman_Garhi" class="mw-redirect" title="Hanuman Garhi">Hanuman Garhi</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-288" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-288">&#91;277&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Soon after Modi returned to power in 2019, he took three actions the RSS had long called for.<sup id="cite_ref-Bhatty_Sundar_pp._632–650_272-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bhatty_Sundar_pp._632–650-272">&#91;261&#93;</a></sup> The practice of <a href="/wiki/Triple_talaq_in_India" title="Triple talaq in India">Triple Talaq</a> was made illegal and became a punishable act from 1 August 2019.<sup id="cite_ref-289" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-289">&#91;278&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-290" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-290">&#91;279&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-291" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-291">&#91;280&#93;</a></sup> The administration repealed <a href="/wiki/Article_370" class="mw-redirect" title="Article 370">Article 370</a> of the Indian constitution that granted autonomy to <a href="/wiki/Jammu_and_Kashmir_(state)" title="Jammu and Kashmir (state)">Jammu and Kashmir</a>, and also <a href="/wiki/The_Jammu_and_Kashmir_Reorganisation_Act,_2019" class="mw-redirect" title="The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019">abrogated its statehood</a>, reorganizing it into the <a href="/wiki/Union_territory" title="Union territory">union territories</a> <a href="/wiki/Jammu_and_Kashmir_(union_territory)" title="Jammu and Kashmir (union territory)">Jammu and Kashmir</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Ladakh" title="Ladakh">Ladakh</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Bhatty_Sundar_pp._632–650_272-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bhatty_Sundar_pp._632–650-272">&#91;261&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:6_292-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:6-292">&#91;281&#93;</a></sup> The region was placed under <a href="/wiki/2019%E2%80%932021_Jammu_and_Kashmir_lockdown" title="2019–2021 Jammu and Kashmir lockdown">a lockdown</a> and internet services were suspended and were not completely restored until February 2021.<sup id="cite_ref-293" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-293">&#91;282&#93;</a></sup> Thousands of people, including hundreds of political leaders, were detained.<sup id="cite_ref-294" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-294">&#91;283&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-295" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-295">&#91;284&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-296" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-296">&#91;285&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-reuters_297-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-reuters-297">&#91;286&#93;</a></sup> The Supreme Court of India did not hear constitutional challenges to the reorganisation or the Citizenship Amendment Act. According to Bhatty and Sundar, this is an example of the subversion of the Supreme Court and other major institutions, which were filled with appointees favouring the BJP.<sup id="cite_ref-Bhatty_Sundar_pp._632–650_272-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bhatty_Sundar_pp._632–650-272">&#91;261&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Economic_policy">Economic policy</span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Informal_meeting_of_the_BRICS_during_the_2019_G20_Osaka_summit.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Informal_meeting_of_the_BRICS_during_the_2019_G20_Osaka_summit.jpg/220px-Informal_meeting_of_the_BRICS_during_the_2019_G20_Osaka_summit.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Informal_meeting_of_the_BRICS_during_the_2019_G20_Osaka_summit.jpg/330px-Informal_meeting_of_the_BRICS_during_the_2019_G20_Osaka_summit.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Informal_meeting_of_the_BRICS_during_the_2019_G20_Osaka_summit.jpg/440px-Informal_meeting_of_the_BRICS_during_the_2019_G20_Osaka_summit.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3506" data-file-height="2337" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/BRICS" title="BRICS">BRICS</a> leaders in 2019. Left to right: <a href="/wiki/Xi_Jinping" title="Xi Jinping">Xi</a> (China), <a href="/wiki/Vladimir_Putin" title="Vladimir Putin">Putin</a> (Russia), <a href="/wiki/Jair_Bolsonaro" title="Jair Bolsonaro">Bolsonaro</a> (Brazil), Modi and <a href="/wiki/Cyril_Ramaphosa" title="Cyril Ramaphosa">Ramaphosa</a> (South Africa)</figcaption></figure>
<p>The Modi government's economic policies focused on privatisation and liberalisation of the economy, and were based on a <a href="/wiki/Neoliberal" class="mw-redirect" title="Neoliberal">neoliberal</a> framework.<sup id="cite_ref-Ruparelia_251-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ruparelia-251">&#91;240&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Shah_&amp;_Lerche_298-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Shah_&amp;_Lerche-298">&#91;287&#93;</a></sup> Modi liberalised India's <a href="/wiki/Foreign_direct_investment" title="Foreign direct investment">foreign direct investment</a> policies, allowing more foreign investment in several industries, including defence and railways.<sup id="cite_ref-Ruparelia_251-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ruparelia-251">&#91;240&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-299" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-299">&#91;288&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-300" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-300">&#91;289&#93;</a></sup> Other proposed reforms included making the forming of unions more difficult for workers, and making recruitment and dismissal easier for employers;<sup id="cite_ref-Shah_&amp;_Lerche_298-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Shah_&amp;_Lerche-298">&#91;287&#93;</a></sup> some of these proposals were abandoned after protests.<sup id="cite_ref-ET_March_2018_301-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ET_March_2018-301">&#91;290&#93;</a></sup> The reforms drew strong opposition from unions; on 2 September 2015, eleven of the country's largest unions—including one affiliated with the BJP—struck.<sup id="cite_ref-Shah_&amp;_Lerche_298-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Shah_&amp;_Lerche-298">&#91;287&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Bharatiya_Mazdoor_Sangh" title="Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh">Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh</a> (Indian Workers Union), a constituent of the <a href="/wiki/Sangh_Parivar" title="Sangh Parivar">Sangh Parivar</a> (Family of the RSS), stated the underlying motivation of labour reforms favoured corporations over labourers.<sup id="cite_ref-Ruparelia_251-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ruparelia-251">&#91;240&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The funds dedicated to poverty-reduction programmes and social welfare measures were greatly reduced by Modi's administration.<sup id="cite_ref-Manor_168-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Manor-168">&#91;157&#93;</a></sup> The money spent on social programmes declined from 14.6 percent of GDP during the previous Congress government to 12.6 percent during Modi's first year in office, and spending on health and family welfare declined by 15 percent.<sup id="cite_ref-Ruparelia_251-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ruparelia-251">&#91;240&#93;</a></sup> The government lowered corporate taxes, abolished the <a href="/wiki/Wealth_Tax_Act,_1957" title="Wealth Tax Act, 1957">wealth tax</a>, increased sales taxes, and reduced customs duties on gold and jewellery.<sup id="cite_ref-Ruparelia_251-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ruparelia-251">&#91;240&#93;</a></sup> In October 2014, the Modi government deregulated diesel prices.<sup id="cite_ref-302" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-302">&#91;291&#93;</a></sup> During Modi's first term, his government reduced spending on education as share of the budget; over five years, education spending dropped from 0.7 percent of GDP to 0.5 percent.<sup id="cite_ref-India_Today_2020_303-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-India_Today_2020-303">&#91;292&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Standard_2018_304-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Standard_2018-304">&#91;293&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Chowdhury_2019_305-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Chowdhury_2019-305">&#91;294&#93;</a></sup> The percentage of the budget spent on children's nutrition, education, health, and associated programmes was almost halved between 2014 and 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-The_Wire_2021_306-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-The_Wire_2021-306">&#91;295&#93;</a></sup> Capital expenditure on transport infrastructure significantly rose, increasing from less than 0.4 percent of GDP in 2014 to 1.7 percent in 2023.<sup id="cite_ref-307" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-307">&#91;296&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In September 2014, Modi introduced the <a href="/wiki/Make_in_India" title="Make in India">Make in India</a> initiative to encourage foreign companies to manufacture products in India with the goal of turning the country into a global manufacturing hub.<sup id="cite_ref-Ruparelia_251-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ruparelia-251">&#91;240&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-308" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-308">&#91;297&#93;</a></sup> Supporters of economic liberalisation supported the initiative but critics said it would allow foreign corporations to capture a greater share of the Indian market.<sup id="cite_ref-Ruparelia_251-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ruparelia-251">&#91;240&#93;</a></sup> Modi's administration passed a land-reform bill that allowed it to acquire private agricultural land without conducting a social impact assessment, and without the consent of the farmers who owned it.<sup id="cite_ref-309" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-309">&#91;298&#93;</a></sup> The bill was passed via an executive order after it faced opposition in Parliament but was eventually allowed to lapse.<sup id="cite_ref-Ronojoy_248-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ronojoy-248">&#91;237&#93;</a></sup> Modi's government passed the <a href="/wiki/Goods_and_Services_Tax_(India)" title="Goods and Services Tax (India)">Goods and Services Tax</a>, the biggest tax reform in the country since independence, subsuming around 17 taxes and became effective on 1 July 2017.<sup id="cite_ref-310" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-310">&#91;299&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Narendra_Modi_launches_Make_in_India.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/Narendra_Modi_launches_Make_in_India.jpg/220px-Narendra_Modi_launches_Make_in_India.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="98" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/Narendra_Modi_launches_Make_in_India.jpg/330px-Narendra_Modi_launches_Make_in_India.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/Narendra_Modi_launches_Make_in_India.jpg/440px-Narendra_Modi_launches_Make_in_India.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2200" data-file-height="984" /></a><figcaption>Modi at the launch of the <a href="/wiki/Make_in_India" title="Make in India">Make in India</a> programme</figcaption></figure>
<p>In his first cabinet decision, Modi set up a team to investigate <a href="/wiki/Black_money" class="mw-redirect" title="Black money">black money</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-311" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-311">&#91;300&#93;</a></sup> On 9 November 2016, the government <a href="/wiki/2016_Indian_banknote_demonetisation" title="2016 Indian banknote demonetisation">demonetised ₹500 and ₹1000 banknotes</a> with the intention of curbing corruption, black money, terrorism and the use of counterfeit currency.<sup id="cite_ref-312" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-312">&#91;301&#93;</a></sup> The move led to severe cash shortages,<sup id="cite_ref-313" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-313">&#91;302&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-314" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-314">&#91;303&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-315" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-315">&#91;304&#93;</a></sup> and a steep decline in the Indian stock indices <a href="/wiki/BSE_SENSEX" title="BSE SENSEX">BSE SENSEX</a> and <a href="/wiki/NIFTY_50" title="NIFTY 50">NIFTY 50</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-316" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-316">&#91;305&#93;</a></sup> and sparked widespread protests throughout the country.<sup id="cite_ref-317" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-317">&#91;306&#93;</a></sup> It is estimated 1.5 million jobs were lost and that one percent of the country's GDP was wiped out.<sup id="cite_ref-theguardian.com_318-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-theguardian.com-318">&#91;307&#93;</a></sup> Several deaths were linked to the rush to exchange cash.<sup id="cite_ref-Aljazeera-1_319-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Aljazeera-1-319">&#91;308&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-320" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-320">&#91;309&#93;</a></sup> In the subsequent year, the number of income tax returns filed for individuals rose by 25 percent and the number of digital transactions steeply increased.<sup id="cite_ref-321" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-321">&#91;310&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-322" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-322">&#91;311&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Modi's administration has observed a decline in GDP growth and increasing joblessness compared to the previous administration under <a href="/wiki/Manmohan_Singh" title="Manmohan Singh">Manmohan Singh</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Inamdar_Alluri_323-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Inamdar_Alluri-323">&#91;312&#93;</a></sup> During the first eight years of Modi's premiership, India's GDP grew at an average rate of 5.5% percent compared tho the rate of 7.03 percent under the previous government.<sup id="cite_ref-Tiwari_2022_324-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Tiwari_2022-324">&#91;313&#93;</a></sup> Income inequality increased;<sup id="cite_ref-CNBC_Nov_2018_325-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CNBC_Nov_2018-325">&#91;314&#93;</a></sup> an internal government report said in 2017, unemployment increased to its highest level in 45 years. The loss of jobs was attributed to the 2016 banknote demonetisation, and the effects of the <a href="/wiki/Goods_and_Services_Tax_(India)" title="Goods and Services Tax (India)">Goods and Services Tax</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-NYT_Jan_2019_326-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NYT_Jan_2019-326">&#91;315&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Reuters_Jan_2019_327-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Reuters_Jan_2019-327">&#91;316&#93;</a></sup> GDP growth was 6.12 percent in the 2018–19 <a href="/wiki/Financial_year" class="mw-redirect" title="Financial year">financial year</a>, with an inflation rate of 3.4 percent.<sup id="cite_ref-328" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-328">&#91;317&#93;</a></sup> In the year 2019–20, the <a href="/wiki/GDP" class="mw-redirect" title="GDP">GDP</a> growth rate slowed to 4.18 percent, while inflation increased to 4.7 percent.<sup id="cite_ref-329" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-329">&#91;318&#93;</a></sup> The Indian economy shrunk by 6.6 percent during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020–21, and was estimated to grow at 8.2 percent the following financial year.<sup id="cite_ref-330" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-330">&#91;319&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Health_and_sanitation">Health and sanitation</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Swachh_Bharat_Mission" title="Swachh Bharat Mission">Swachh Bharat Mission</a></div>
<p>In his first year as prime minister, Modi reduced the central government's healthcare spending.<sup id="cite_ref-Economist_2015_201-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Economist_2015-201">&#91;190&#93;</a></sup> In January 2015, the Modi government launched its New Health Policy (NHP), which did not increase the government's spending on healthcare but emphasised the role of private healthcare organisations. This represented a shift away from the policy of the previous Congress government, which had supported programmes to assist public health goals, including a reduction in child and maternal mortality rates.<sup id="cite_ref-Lancet_331-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Lancet-331">&#91;320&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/National_Health_Mission" title="National Health Mission">National Health Mission</a>, which included public health programmes targeted at these indices, received nearly 20 percent less funding<sup id="cite_ref-332" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-332">&#91;321&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-333" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-333">&#91;322&#93;</a></sup> in 2015 than in the previous year. The Modi administration reduced the healthcare budget by a further 15% in its second year.<sup id="cite_ref-334" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-334">&#91;323&#93;</a></sup> The healthcare budget for the following year rose by 19%; private insurance providers positively viewed the budget but public health experts criticised its emphasis on the role of private healthcare providers and said it represented a shift away from public health facilities.<sup id="cite_ref-335" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-335">&#91;324&#93;</a></sup> The healthcare budget rose by 11.5% in 2018; the change included an allocation of <span class="nowrap"><span style="white-space: nowrap">₹</span>20 billion</span> (US$250&#160;million) for a <a href="/wiki/Ayushman_Bharat_Yojana" title="Ayushman Bharat Yojana">government-funded health insurance program</a> and a decrease in the budget of the <a href="/wiki/National_Health_Mission" title="National Health Mission">National Health Mission</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-336" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-336">&#91;325&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:The_Prime_Minister,_Shri_Narendra_Modi_interacting_with_the_Chief_Ministers_via_video_conferencing_to_discuss_the_situation_emerging_post_Unlock_1.0_and_plan_ahead_for_tackling_the_COVID-19_pandemic,_in_New_Delhi_on_June_16,_2020.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_interacting_with_the_Chief_Ministers_via_video_conferencing_to_discuss_the_situation_emerging_post_Unlock_1.0_and_plan_ahead_for_tackling_the_COVID-19_pandemic%2C_in_New_Delhi_on_June_16%2C_2020.jpg/220px-thumbnail.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="144" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_interacting_with_the_Chief_Ministers_via_video_conferencing_to_discuss_the_situation_emerging_post_Unlock_1.0_and_plan_ahead_for_tackling_the_COVID-19_pandemic%2C_in_New_Delhi_on_June_16%2C_2020.jpg/330px-thumbnail.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_interacting_with_the_Chief_Ministers_via_video_conferencing_to_discuss_the_situation_emerging_post_Unlock_1.0_and_plan_ahead_for_tackling_the_COVID-19_pandemic%2C_in_New_Delhi_on_June_16%2C_2020.jpg/440px-thumbnail.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2200" data-file-height="1443" /></a><figcaption>Modi discussing the COVID-19 pandemic with Chief Ministers via videoconferencing in June 2020</figcaption></figure>
<p>Modi emphasised his government's efforts at sanitation as a means of ensuring good health.<sup id="cite_ref-Lancet_331-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Lancet-331">&#91;320&#93;</a></sup> On 2 October 2014, Modi launched the <a href="/wiki/Swachh_Bharat_Mission" title="Swachh Bharat Mission">Swachh Bharat Mission</a> ("Clean India") campaign. The campaign's stated goals included the elimination of <a href="/wiki/Open_defecation" title="Open defecation">open defecation</a> and <a href="/wiki/Manual_scavenging" title="Manual scavenging">manual scavenging</a> within five years.<sup id="cite_ref-337" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-337">&#91;326&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Clean_India_338-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Clean_India-338">&#91;327&#93;</a></sup> As part of the programme, the Indian government began constructing millions of toilets in rural areas and encouraging people to use them.<sup id="cite_ref-Lakshmi_339-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Lakshmi-339">&#91;328&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Gahlot_340-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Gahlot-340">&#91;329&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-341" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-341">&#91;330&#93;</a></sup> The government also announced plans to build new sewage treatment plants,<sup id="cite_ref-342" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-342">&#91;331&#93;</a></sup> and planned to construct 60&#160;million toilets by 2019. The construction projects faced allegations of corruption and severe difficulty in getting people to use the newly constructed toilets.<sup id="cite_ref-Clean_India_338-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Clean_India-338">&#91;327&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Lakshmi_339-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Lakshmi-339">&#91;328&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Gahlot_340-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Gahlot-340">&#91;329&#93;</a></sup> Sanitation cover in India increased from 38.7% in October 2014 to 84.1% in May 2018 but use of the new sanitary facilities was lower than the government's targets.<sup id="cite_ref-343" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-343">&#91;332&#93;</a></sup> In 2018, the <a href="/wiki/World_Health_Organization" title="World Health Organization">World Health Organization</a> (WHO) stated at least 180,000 diarrhoeal deaths in rural India were averted after the launch of the sanitation effort.<sup id="cite_ref-344" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-344">&#91;333&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In March 2020, in response to the <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_India" title="COVID-19 pandemic in India">COVID-19 pandemic</a>, the Modi administration invoked the <a href="/wiki/Epidemic_Diseases_Act,_1897" title="Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897">Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897</a> and <a href="/wiki/Disaster_Management_Act,_2005" title="Disaster Management Act, 2005">Disaster Management Act, 2005</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-345" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-345">&#91;334&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:04_346-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:04-346">&#91;335&#93;</a></sup> The same month, all commercial domestic and international flights were suspended.<sup id="cite_ref-:210_347-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:210-347">&#91;336&#93;</a></sup> Modi announced a 14-hour curfew on 22 March,<sup id="cite_ref-348" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-348">&#91;337&#93;</a></sup> and followed with a three-week "total lockdown" two days later.<sup id="cite_ref-:192_349-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:192-349">&#91;338&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-350" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-350">&#91;339&#93;</a></sup> Restrictions were gradually lifted beginning in April, and were completely revoked in November 2020.<sup id="cite_ref-:210_347-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:210-347">&#91;336&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:Unlock5PDF_351-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:Unlock5PDF-351">&#91;340&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-352" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-352">&#91;341&#93;</a></sup> A second wave of the pandemic that began in March 2021 was significantly more devastating than the first; some parts of India experienced shortages of vaccines, hospital beds, <a href="/wiki/Gas_cylinder" title="Gas cylinder">oxygen cylinders</a> and other medical supplies.<sup id="cite_ref-:0b_353-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0b-353">&#91;342&#93;</a></sup> In late April India reported over 400,000 cases in a 24-hour period, the first country to do so.<sup id="cite_ref-354" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-354">&#91;343&#93;</a></sup> India began its <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_vaccination_in_India" title="COVID-19 vaccination in India">vaccination programme</a> in January 2021;<sup id="cite_ref-:7_355-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:7-355">&#91;344&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-356" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-356">&#91;345&#93;</a></sup> in January 2022, India announced it had administered about 1.7 billion doses of vaccines and that more than 720 million people were fully vaccinated.<sup id="cite_ref-UNSDG_357-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-UNSDG-357">&#91;346&#93;</a></sup> In May 2022, the WHO estimated 4.7 million people had died of COVID-19 in India, mostly during the second wave in mid 2021—almost 10 times the Indian government's estimate. The Modi administration rejected the WHO's estimate.<sup id="cite_ref-WHO_estimate_30-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-WHO_estimate-30">&#91;24&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Biswas_2022_31-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Biswas_2022-31">&#91;25&#93;</a></sup> India's death toll was thus the highest worldwide, accounting for more than 20% of all Covid deaths.<sup id="cite_ref-Jones_2023_pp._131–147_358-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jones_2023_pp._131–147-358">&#91;347&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Foreign_policy">Foreign policy</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Foreign_policy_of_Narendra_Modi" class="mw-redirect" title="Foreign policy of Narendra Modi">Foreign policy of Narendra Modi</a> and <a href="/wiki/List_of_international_prime_ministerial_trips_made_by_Narendra_Modi" title="List of international prime ministerial trips made by Narendra Modi">trips as prime minister</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:TrumpModi.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/TrumpModi.jpg/220px-TrumpModi.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="141" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/TrumpModi.jpg/330px-TrumpModi.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/TrumpModi.jpg/440px-TrumpModi.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1023" data-file-height="654" /></a><figcaption>Modi with U.S. President <a href="/wiki/Donald_Trump" title="Donald Trump">Donald Trump</a> at <a href="/wiki/Namaste_Trump" title="Namaste Trump">Namaste Trump</a> rally in <a href="/wiki/Ahmedabad" title="Ahmedabad">Ahmedabad</a>, India</figcaption></figure>
<p>Foreign policy played a small role in Modi's election campaign and did not feature prominently in the BJP's election manifesto.<sup id="cite_ref-Hall_2015_359-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Hall_2015-359">&#91;348&#93;</a></sup> Modi's foreign policy, similarly to that of the preceding Congress government, focused on improving economic ties, security and regional relations.<sup id="cite_ref-Hall_2015_359-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Hall_2015-359">&#91;348&#93;</a></sup> Modi continued Manmohan Singh's policy of "multi-alignment".<sup id="cite_ref-Hall_2015_359-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Hall_2015-359">&#91;348&#93;</a></sup> The Modi administration tried to attract foreign investment in the Indian economy from several sources, especially East Asia, with the use of slogans such as "<a href="/wiki/Make_in_India" title="Make in India">Make in India</a>" and "<a href="/wiki/Digital_India" title="Digital India">Digital India</a>". The government also tried to improve relations with <a href="/wiki/Middle_Eastern_foreign_policy_of_the_Narendra_Modi_government" title="Middle Eastern foreign policy of the Narendra Modi government">Islamic nations in the Middle East</a>, such as <a href="/wiki/Bahrain%E2%80%93India_relations" title="Bahrain–India relations">Bahrain</a>, <a href="/wiki/India%E2%80%93Iran_relations" title="India–Iran relations">Iran</a>, <a href="/wiki/India%E2%80%93Saudi_Arabia_relations" title="India–Saudi Arabia relations">Saudi Arabia</a> and the <a href="/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates_India_relations" class="mw-redirect" title="United Arab Emirates India relations">United Arab Emirates</a>, as well as with <a href="/wiki/India%E2%80%93Israel_relations" title="India–Israel relations">Israel</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-361" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-361">&#91;l&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:The_Vice_President,_Shri_M._Venkaiah_Naidu_and_the_Prime_Minister,_Shri_Narendra_Modi_meeting_the_State_Counsellor_of_Myanmar,_Aung_San_Suu_Kyi,_at_the_Ceremonial_Reception,_at_Rashtrapati_Bhavan,_in_New_Delhi.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9e/The_Vice_President%2C_Shri_M._Venkaiah_Naidu_and_the_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_meeting_the_State_Counsellor_of_Myanmar%2C_Aung_San_Suu_Kyi%2C_at_the_Ceremonial_Reception%2C_at_Rashtrapati_Bhavan%2C_in_New_Delhi.jpg/220px-thumbnail.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="139" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9e/The_Vice_President%2C_Shri_M._Venkaiah_Naidu_and_the_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_meeting_the_State_Counsellor_of_Myanmar%2C_Aung_San_Suu_Kyi%2C_at_the_Ceremonial_Reception%2C_at_Rashtrapati_Bhavan%2C_in_New_Delhi.jpg/330px-thumbnail.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9e/The_Vice_President%2C_Shri_M._Venkaiah_Naidu_and_the_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_meeting_the_State_Counsellor_of_Myanmar%2C_Aung_San_Suu_Kyi%2C_at_the_Ceremonial_Reception%2C_at_Rashtrapati_Bhavan%2C_in_New_Delhi.jpg/440px-thumbnail.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1580" data-file-height="998" /></a><figcaption>Modi meeting <a href="/wiki/Myanmar" title="Myanmar">Myanmar</a>'s leader <a href="/wiki/Aung_San_Suu_Kyi" title="Aung San Suu Kyi">Aung San Suu Kyi</a> in New Delhi in January 2018</figcaption></figure>
<p><a href="/wiki/India-USA_relations" class="mw-redirect" title="India-USA relations">India's relationship with the United States</a> improved after Narendra Modi became PM.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHall2020283–285Gupta20193–9Madan202065_362-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHall2020283–285Gupta20193–9Madan202065-362">&#91;350&#93;</a></sup> During the run-up to the general election, there was wide-ranging scepticism about future of the strategic bilateral relationship under Modi's premiership; in 2005, while <a href="/wiki/Chief_Minister_of_Gujarat" class="mw-redirect" title="Chief Minister of Gujarat">Chief Minister of Gujarat</a>, Modi was denied a US visa during the <a href="/wiki/Presidency_of_George_W._Bush" title="Presidency of George W. Bush">presidency of George W. Bush</a> for his poor human-rights record.<sup id="cite_ref-2005_ban_171-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2005_ban-171">&#91;160&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-visa_denied_172-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-visa_denied-172">&#91;161&#93;</a></sup> Sensing Modi's victory well before the election, <a href="/wiki/United_States_Ambassador_to_India" class="mw-redirect" title="United States Ambassador to India">US Ambassador</a> to India <a href="/wiki/Nancy_Powell" class="mw-redirect" title="Nancy Powell">Nancy Powell</a> contacted Modi as part of greater <i><a href="/wiki/Rapprochement" title="Rapprochement">rapprochement</a></i> from the West. Following Modi's 2014 appointment as India's PM, <a href="/wiki/Presidency_of_Barack_Obama" title="Presidency of Barack Obama">President Obama</a> congratulated him over the telephone and invited Modi to visit the US.<sup id="cite_ref-363" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-363">&#91;351&#93;</a></sup> The Modi government enjoyed a positive relationship with the US during the presidencies of Barack Obama and his successor <a href="/wiki/Donald_Trump" title="Donald Trump">Donald Trump</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-364" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-364">&#91;352&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-365" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-365">&#91;353&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>During the first few months after his appointment as PM, Modi visited a number of countries in support of his policy, and attended the <a href="/wiki/BRICS" title="BRICS">BRICS</a>, <a href="/wiki/ASEAN" title="ASEAN">ASEAN</a> and <a href="/wiki/G20" title="G20">G20</a> summits.<sup id="cite_ref-Hall_2015_359-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Hall_2015-359">&#91;348&#93;</a></sup> One of Modi's first visits as PM was to Nepal, during which he promised one billion US dollars in aid.<sup id="cite_ref-Mocko_366-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Mocko-366">&#91;354&#93;</a></sup> Modi also made several visits to the US;<sup id="cite_ref-Pant_2014_367-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Pant_2014-367">&#91;355&#93;</a></sup> this was described as an unexpected development because of the US's earlier denial of a US travel visa to Modi over his role in the 2002 Gujarat riots. The visits were expected to strengthen diplomatic and trade relations between the two countries.<sup id="cite_ref-Pant_2014_367-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Pant_2014-367">&#91;355&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2015, the Indian parliament ratified a land-exchange deal with Bangladesh in the <a href="/wiki/India%E2%80%93Bangladesh_enclaves" title="India–Bangladesh enclaves">India–Bangladesh enclaves</a>, which the government of Manmohan Singh had initiated.<sup id="cite_ref-Ronojoy_248-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ronojoy-248">&#91;237&#93;</a></sup> Modi's administration brought renewed attention to India's "Look East Policy", which was instituted in 1991. The policy, which was renamed the "Act East Policy", involved directing Indian foreign policy towards East Asia and <a href="/wiki/Southeast_Asia" title="Southeast Asia">Southeast Asia</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Downie_368-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Downie-368">&#91;356&#93;</a></sup> The government signed agreements to improve land connectivity with <a href="/wiki/Myanmar" title="Myanmar">Myanmar</a> through the Indian state of <a href="/wiki/Manipur" title="Manipur">Manipur</a>; this represented a break with India's historic engagement with Myanmar, which prioritised border security over trade.<sup id="cite_ref-Downie_368-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Downie-368">&#91;356&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/China%E2%80%93India_relations" title="China–India relations">China–India relations</a> rapidly deteriorated following the <a href="/wiki/2020_China%E2%80%93India_skirmishes" class="mw-redirect" title="2020 China–India skirmishes">2020 China–India skirmishes</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-369" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-369">&#91;357&#93;</a></sup> Modi pledged aid of $900 million to Afghanistan, which he visited twice and was honoured with Afghanistan's highest civilian honour in 2016.<sup id="cite_ref-370" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-370">&#91;358&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Order_of_Amanullah_Khan_371-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Order_of_Amanullah_Khan-371">&#91;359&#93;</a></sup> In September 2022, Modi appeared to have developed a strong personal relationship with Russia's President <a href="/wiki/Vladimir_Putin" title="Vladimir Putin">Vladimir Putin</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-372" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-372">&#91;360&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-373" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-373">&#91;361&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-374" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-374">&#91;362&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Defence_policy">Defence policy</span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:The_Prime_Minister,_Shri_Narendra_Modi_and_the_Prime_Minister_of_Israel,_Mr._Benjamin_Netanyahu_visiting_the_Technology_Exhibition,_at_Tel_Aviv,_Israel_on_July_06,_2017_(2).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_and_the_Prime_Minister_of_Israel%2C_Mr._Benjamin_Netanyahu_visiting_the_Technology_Exhibition%2C_at_Tel_Aviv%2C_Israel_on_July_06%2C_2017_%282%29.jpg/220px-thumbnail.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_and_the_Prime_Minister_of_Israel%2C_Mr._Benjamin_Netanyahu_visiting_the_Technology_Exhibition%2C_at_Tel_Aviv%2C_Israel_on_July_06%2C_2017_%282%29.jpg/330px-thumbnail.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_and_the_Prime_Minister_of_Israel%2C_Mr._Benjamin_Netanyahu_visiting_the_Technology_Exhibition%2C_at_Tel_Aviv%2C_Israel_on_July_06%2C_2017_%282%29.jpg/440px-thumbnail.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1560" data-file-height="1044" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu" title="Benjamin Netanyahu">Benjamin Netanyahu</a>, <a href="/wiki/List_of_prime_ministers_of_Israel" title="List of prime ministers of Israel">at the time</a> <a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Israel" title="Prime Minister of Israel">Prime Minister of Israel</a>, and Modi visiting the Technology Exhibition, at <a href="/wiki/Tel_Aviv" title="Tel Aviv">Tel Aviv</a>, Israel in 2017</figcaption></figure>
<p>India's nominal military spending steadily increased under Modi.<sup id="cite_ref-Manghat_2019_375-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Manghat_2019-375">&#91;363&#93;</a></sup> During Modi's tenure, the military budget declined, both as a fraction of GDP and when adjusted for inflation.<sup id="cite_ref-Diplomat_2019_376-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Diplomat_2019-376">&#91;364&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Paper_elephant_377-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Paper_elephant-377">&#91;365&#93;</a></sup> A substantial portion of the military budget was devoted to personnel costs commentators wrote the budget was constraining Indian military modernisation.<sup id="cite_ref-Diplomat_2019_376-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Diplomat_2019-376">&#91;364&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Nikkei_2019_378-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Nikkei_2019-378">&#91;366&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Paper_elephant_377-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Paper_elephant-377">&#91;365&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Modi promised to be "tough on Pakistan" during his election campaign and repeatedly called Pakistan an <a href="/wiki/Pakistan_and_state-sponsored_terrorism" title="Pakistan and state-sponsored terrorism">exporter of terrorism</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Reversing_roles_379-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Reversing_roles-379">&#91;367&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-tie0916_380-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-tie0916-380">&#91;368&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-381" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-381">&#91;369&#93;</a></sup> On 29 September 2016, the Modi administration said Indian Army had conducted a <a href="/wiki/2016_Indian_Line_of_Control_strike" title="2016 Indian Line of Control strike">surgical strike</a> on terror <a href="/wiki/Launch_pad" title="Launch pad">launch pads</a> in <a href="/wiki/Azad_Kashmir" title="Azad Kashmir">Azad Kashmir</a>; the Indian media said up to 50 terrorists and Pakistani soldiers had been killed in the strike.<sup id="cite_ref-DGMO_382-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-DGMO-382">&#91;370&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FE_383-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FE-383">&#91;371&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-para_commandos_384-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-para_commandos-384">&#91;372&#93;</a></sup> Pakistan denied any surgical strikes to have taken place.<sup id="cite_ref-385" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-385">&#91;373&#93;</a></sup> Subsequent reports said India's statement about the scope of the strike and the number of casualties had been exaggerated.<sup id="cite_ref-Reversing_roles_379-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Reversing_roles-379">&#91;367&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-truth_386-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-truth-386">&#91;374&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-387" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-387">&#91;375&#93;</a></sup> In February 2019, India carried out <a href="/wiki/2019_Balakot_airstrike" title="2019 Balakot airstrike">airstrikes</a> against a supposed terrorist camp in Pakistan;
