no targets of significance were hit.<sup id="cite_ref-388" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-388">&#91;376&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-389" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-389">&#91;377&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/India%E2%80%93Pakistan_border_skirmishes_(2019)" class="mw-redirect" title="India–Pakistan border skirmishes (2019)">Further military skirmishes</a>, including cross-border shelling and the loss of an Indian aircraft, occurred.<sup id="cite_ref-390" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-390">&#91;378&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-391" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-391">&#91;379&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-392" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-392">&#91;380&#93;</a></sup> Eight months after the incident, the Modi administration admitted that six Indian military personnel had been killed by <a href="/wiki/Friendly_fire" title="Friendly fire">friendly fire</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-friendlyfire_393-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-friendlyfire-393">&#91;381&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:P20210924AS-1147-2_(51707173079).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6b/P20210924AS-1147-2_%2851707173079%29.jpg/220px-P20210924AS-1147-2_%2851707173079%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="135" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6b/P20210924AS-1147-2_%2851707173079%29.jpg/330px-P20210924AS-1147-2_%2851707173079%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6b/P20210924AS-1147-2_%2851707173079%29.jpg/440px-P20210924AS-1147-2_%2851707173079%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3000" data-file-height="1843" /></a><figcaption>PM Modi along with <a href="/wiki/Quadrilateral_Security_Dialogue" title="Quadrilateral Security Dialogue">Quad</a> leaders in Washington</figcaption></figure>
<p>In May 2020, Chinese and Indian troops engaged in an aggressive skirmishes along the <a href="/wiki/Sino-Indian_border" class="mw-redirect" title="Sino-Indian border">Sino-Indian border</a>, including near the disputed <a href="/wiki/Pangong_Lake" class="mw-redirect" title="Pangong Lake">Pangong Lake</a>, <a href="/wiki/Ladakh" title="Ladakh">Ladakh</a>, and the <a href="/wiki/Tibet_Autonomous_Region" title="Tibet Autonomous Region">Tibet Autonomous Region</a>; and near the border between <a href="/wiki/Sikkim" title="Sikkim">Sikkim</a> and the Tibet Autonomous Region. Additional clashes took place in eastern Ladakh along the <a href="/wiki/Line_of_Actual_Control" title="Line of Actual Control">Line of Actual Control</a> (LAC).<sup id="cite_ref-394" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-394">&#91;382&#93;</a></sup> In 2020, <a href="/wiki/2020_India-China_skirmishes" class="mw-redirect" title="2020 India-China skirmishes">skirmishes</a> between the nations led to many border clashes, responses and reactions from both sides.<sup id="cite_ref-395" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-395">&#91;383&#93;</a></sup> A series of talks between India and China were held, using military and diplomatic means for peace.<sup id="cite_ref-396" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-396">&#91;384&#93;</a></sup> The first border clash reported in 2021 was on 20 January; this was referred to as a minor border clash in Sikkim.<sup id="cite_ref-397" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-397">&#91;385&#93;</a></sup> Modi has been criticized for maintaining silence over <a href="/wiki/2020%E2%80%932021_China%E2%80%93India_skirmishes#India&#39;s_territorial_loss" title="2020–2021 China–India skirmishes">ceding</a> about 2,000 sq km land to China since June 2020.<sup id="cite_ref-guardian_398-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-guardian-398">&#91;386&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Siddiqui_399-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Siddiqui-399">&#91;387&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-BrahmaChellaney_400-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-BrahmaChellaney-400">&#91;388&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In December 2021, Modi signed an agreement with Russian leader Vladimir Putin to extend military technical cooperation.<sup id="cite_ref-:12_401-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:12-401">&#91;389&#93;</a></sup> The Modi government bought the <a href="/wiki/S-400_missile_system" title="S-400 missile system">S-400 missile system</a>, an anti-missile striking system, strengthening the relationship between the two nations.<sup id="cite_ref-402" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-402">&#91;390&#93;</a></sup> India refused to condemn the <a href="/wiki/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" class="mw-redirect" title="2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine">2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine</a> and stayed neutral.<sup id="cite_ref-:12_401-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:12-401">&#91;389&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-403" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-403">&#91;391&#93;</a></sup> The Indian government's <a href="/wiki/Operation_Ganga" title="Operation Ganga">Operation Ganga</a> initiative sought to return Indians stranded in Ukraine during the war. More than 19,000 Indian nationals were evacuated,<sup id="cite_ref-404" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-404">&#91;392&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-405" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-405">&#91;393&#93;</a></sup> including some from neighbouring countries.<sup id="cite_ref-406" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-406">&#91;394&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Environmental_policy">Environmental policy</span></h3>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Prime_Minister_Narendra_Modi_at_India_Pavilion_in_Paris_during_COP21_(23193999974).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/Prime_Minister_Narendra_Modi_at_India_Pavilion_in_Paris_during_COP21_%2823193999974%29.jpg/244px-Prime_Minister_Narendra_Modi_at_India_Pavilion_in_Paris_during_COP21_%2823193999974%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="244" height="157" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/Prime_Minister_Narendra_Modi_at_India_Pavilion_in_Paris_during_COP21_%2823193999974%29.jpg/366px-Prime_Minister_Narendra_Modi_at_India_Pavilion_in_Paris_during_COP21_%2823193999974%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/Prime_Minister_Narendra_Modi_at_India_Pavilion_in_Paris_during_COP21_%2823193999974%29.jpg/488px-Prime_Minister_Narendra_Modi_at_India_Pavilion_in_Paris_during_COP21_%2823193999974%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2200" data-file-height="1412" /></a><figcaption>Modi (right) at <a href="/wiki/CoP21_Climate_Conference" class="mw-redirect" title="CoP21 Climate Conference">CoP21 Climate Conference</a>, in Paris, announcing the founding of an International <a href="/wiki/Solar_Alliance" class="mw-redirect" title="Solar Alliance">Solar Alliance</a> (ISA). November 2015.</figcaption></figure>
<p>While naming his cabinet, Modi renamed the Ministry of Environment and Forests the "Ministry of Environment, Forests, and Climate Change", and more-than-halved its money allocation in his administration's first budget.<sup id="cite_ref-407" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-407">&#91;395&#93;</a></sup> The new ministry removed or diluted a number of laws related to environmental protection, and others related to industrial activity.<sup id="cite_ref-Ruparelia_251-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ruparelia-251">&#91;240&#93;</a></sup> The government also tried to reconstitute the <a href="/wiki/National_Board_for_Wildlife" class="mw-redirect" title="National Board for Wildlife">National Board for Wildlife</a> so it would no longer have representatives from NGOs but the <a href="/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_India" title="Supreme Court of India">Supreme Court of India</a> blocked this move.<sup id="cite_ref-Kothari_408-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Kothari-408">&#91;396&#93;</a></sup> Other changes included a reduction of ministry oversight on small mining projects and ending the requirement for approval from tribal councils for projects inside forested areas. Modi also lifted a moratorium on new industrial activity in India's most-polluted areas.<sup id="cite_ref-Kothari_408-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Kothari-408">&#91;396&#93;</a></sup> The changes were welcomed by businesspeople but criticised by environmentalists.<sup id="cite_ref-409" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-409">&#91;397&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Speaking with <a href="/wiki/Assamese_people" title="Assamese people">Assamese</a> students in 2014, Modi downplayed <a href="/wiki/Climate_change" title="Climate change">climate change</a>, saying; "Climate has not changed. We have changed. Our habits have changed. Our habits have got spoiled. Due to that, we have destroyed our entire environment."<sup id="cite_ref-410" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-410">&#91;398&#93;</a></sup> Later in his administration, however, he has called for <a href="/wiki/Climate_action" title="Climate action">climate action</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-411" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-411">&#91;399&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-412" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-412">&#91;400&#93;</a></sup> especially with the proliferation of <a href="/wiki/Clean_energy" class="mw-redirect" title="Clean energy">clean energy</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-413" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-413">&#91;401&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-414" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-414">&#91;402&#93;</a></sup> In 2015, Modi proposed the <a href="/wiki/International_Solar_Alliance" title="International Solar Alliance">International Solar Alliance</a> initiative to encourage investment in solar energy.<sup id="cite_ref-415" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-415">&#91;403&#93;</a></sup> Holding developed countries responsible,<sup id="cite_ref-416" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-416">&#91;404&#93;</a></sup> Modi and his government have said India has had a negligible historical role in climate change. At the <a href="/wiki/COP26" class="mw-redirect" title="COP26">COP26</a> conference, Modi announced India would target <a href="/wiki/Carbon_neutrality" class="mw-redirect" title="Carbon neutrality">carbon neutrality</a> by 2070 and expand its renewable energy capacity.<sup id="cite_ref-417" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-417">&#91;405&#93;</a></sup> Indian environmentalists and economists applauded the decision, describing it as bold climate action.<sup id="cite_ref-418" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-418">&#91;406&#93;</a></sup> India has become the only major economy to be on track to meet its <a href="/wiki/Paris_Agreement" title="Paris Agreement">Paris Agreement</a> goals.<sup id="cite_ref-419" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-419">&#91;407&#93;</a></sup> It has achieved 10 percent of ethanol blending five months ahead of schedule.<sup id="cite_ref-420" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-420">&#91;408&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Democratic_backsliding">Democratic backsliding</span></h3>
<p>Under Modi's tenure, India has experienced <a href="/wiki/Democratic_backsliding" title="Democratic backsliding">democratic backsliding</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-lo9_39-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-lo9-39">&#91;g&#93;</a></sup> According to one study, "The BJP government incrementally but systemically attacked nearly all existing mechanisms that are in place to hold the political executive to account, either by ensuring that these mechanisms became subservient to the political executive or were captured by party loyalists".<sup id="cite_ref-:2_35-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-35">&#91;29&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-421" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-421">&#91;409&#93;</a></sup> The Modi government has used state power to intimidate and stifle critics in the media and academia, undermining freedom of expression and alternative sources of information.<sup id="cite_ref-:3_422-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-422">&#91;410&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:4_36-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:4-36">&#91;30&#93;</a></sup> His administration has been criticised for using a democratic mandate to undermine democratic processes, including focusing on Hindu-nationalist priorities rather than economic development. Modi's second term as PM, in particular, saw the erosion of civil rights and <a href="/wiki/Freedom_of_the_press_in_India" title="Freedom of the press in India">press freedom</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-423" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-423">&#91;411&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Public_perception_and_image">Public perception and image</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Public_image_of_Narendra_Modi" title="Public image of Narendra Modi">Public image of Narendra Modi</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:The_Prime_Minister,_Shri_Narendra_Modi_participates_in_the_mass_yoga_demonstration_at_Rajpath_on_the_occasion_of_International_Yoga_Day,_in_New_Delhi_on_June_21,_2015.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/82/The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_participates_in_the_mass_yoga_demonstration_at_Rajpath_on_the_occasion_of_International_Yoga_Day%2C_in_New_Delhi_on_June_21%2C_2015.jpg/220px-thumbnail.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="119" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/82/The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_participates_in_the_mass_yoga_demonstration_at_Rajpath_on_the_occasion_of_International_Yoga_Day%2C_in_New_Delhi_on_June_21%2C_2015.jpg/330px-thumbnail.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/82/The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_participates_in_the_mass_yoga_demonstration_at_Rajpath_on_the_occasion_of_International_Yoga_Day%2C_in_New_Delhi_on_June_21%2C_2015.jpg/440px-thumbnail.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2150" data-file-height="1163" /></a><figcaption>Modi at <a href="/wiki/International_Yoga_Day" class="mw-redirect" title="International Yoga Day">Yoga Day</a> celebrations in New Delhi, 21 June 2015</figcaption></figure>
<p>Narendra Modi has received <a href="/wiki/Opinion_polling_on_the_Narendra_Modi_premiership" title="Opinion polling on the Narendra Modi premiership">consistently high approval ratings</a> during his premiership;<sup id="cite_ref-:0_40-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-40">&#91;33&#93;</a></sup> he is often <a href="/wiki/Historical_rankings_of_prime_ministers_of_India" class="mw-redirect" title="Historical rankings of prime ministers of India">ranked</a> in popular opinion polls as the greatest prime minister in Indian history.<sup id="cite_ref-:5_424-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:5-424">&#91;412&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:8_425-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:8-425">&#91;413&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:1_426-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1-426">&#91;414&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Image">Image</span></h3>
<p>Modi is a <a href="/wiki/Vegetarianism" title="Vegetarianism">vegetarian</a> and <a href="/wiki/Teetotaler" class="mw-redirect" title="Teetotaler">teetotaler</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-427" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-427">&#91;415&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-428" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-428">&#91;416&#93;</a></sup> who has a frugal lifestyle, and is a <a href="/wiki/Workaholic" title="Workaholic">workaholic</a> and <a href="/wiki/Introversion" class="mw-redirect" title="Introversion">introvert</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-429" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-429">&#91;417&#93;</a></sup> On 31 August 2012, he posted on <a href="/wiki/Google_Hangouts" title="Google Hangouts">Google Hangouts</a>, becoming the first Indian politician to interact with citizens on a live chat.<sup id="cite_ref-toi_430-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-toi-430">&#91;418&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-ibn_431-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ibn-431">&#91;419&#93;</a></sup> Modi has been called a fashion icon for his signature crisply ironed, half-sleeved <i><a href="/wiki/Kurta" title="Kurta">kurta</a></i>, and for a suit with his name repeatedly embroidered in the pinstripes, which he wore during a state visit by US President <a href="/wiki/Barack_Obama" title="Barack Obama">Barack Obama</a>, which drew public and media attention, and criticism.<sup id="cite_ref-Sharma_June_2014_432-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Sharma_June_2014-432">&#91;420&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Friedman_June_2014_433-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Friedman_June_2014-433">&#91;421&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Price_434-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Price-434">&#91;422&#93;</a></sup> Scholars and biographers have described Modi's personality as energetic, arrogant and charismatic.<sup id="cite_ref-Stepan_44-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Stepan-44">&#91;37&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEMarino201460–70_435-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMarino201460–70-435">&#91;423&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The nomination of Modi for the prime-ministership drew attention to his reputation as "one of contemporary India's most controversial and divisive politicians".<sup id="cite_ref-Basu_2014_195-5" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Basu_2014-195">&#91;184&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-436" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-436">&#91;424&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-437" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-437">&#91;425&#93;</a></sup> During the 2014 election campaign, the BJP projected an image of Modi as a strong, masculine leader who would be able to take difficult decisions.<sup id="cite_ref-Basu_2014_195-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Basu_2014-195">&#91;184&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Chhibber_215-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Chhibber-215">&#91;204&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Jaffrelot_2015_217-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jaffrelot_2015-217">&#91;206&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Chacko_221-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Chacko-221">&#91;210&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Srivastava_222-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Srivastava-222">&#91;211&#93;</a></sup> Campaigns in which he has participated have focused on Modi as an individual, a unusual tactic for the BJP and RSS.<sup id="cite_ref-Jaffrelot_2015_217-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jaffrelot_2015-217">&#91;206&#93;</a></sup> Modi has relied upon his reputation as a politician able to bring about economic growth and development.<sup id="cite_ref-et20130715_438-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-et20130715-438">&#91;426&#93;</a></sup> Modi's role in the 2002 Gujarat riots continues to attract criticism and controversy.<sup id="cite_ref-Buncombe_11-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Buncombe-11">&#91;8&#93;</a></sup> Modi's hardline Hindutva philosophy and the policies adopted by his government also continue to draw criticism, and have been seen as evidence of a majoritarian and exclusionary social agenda.<sup id="cite_ref-Buncombe_11-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Buncombe-11">&#91;8&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Stepan_44-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Stepan-44">&#91;37&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Manor_168-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Manor-168">&#91;157&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Jaffrelot_2015_217-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jaffrelot_2015-217">&#91;206&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Approval_ratings">Approval ratings</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Opinion_polling_on_the_Narendra_Modi_premiership" title="Opinion polling on the Narendra Modi premiership">Opinion polling on the Narendra Modi premiership</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:The_Prime_Minister,_Shri_Narendra_Modi_interacting_with_the_school_children_after_addressing_the_Nation,_on_the_occasion_of_71st_Independence_Day_from_the_ramparts_of_Red_Fort,_in_Delhi_on_August_15,_2017.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_interacting_with_the_school_children_after_addressing_the_Nation%2C_on_the_occasion_of_71st_Independence_Day_from_the_ramparts_of_Red_Fort%2C_in_Delhi_on_August_15%2C_2017.jpg/220px-thumbnail.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_interacting_with_the_school_children_after_addressing_the_Nation%2C_on_the_occasion_of_71st_Independence_Day_from_the_ramparts_of_Red_Fort%2C_in_Delhi_on_August_15%2C_2017.jpg/330px-thumbnail.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/The_Prime_Minister%2C_Shri_Narendra_Modi_interacting_with_the_school_children_after_addressing_the_Nation%2C_on_the_occasion_of_71st_Independence_Day_from_the_ramparts_of_Red_Fort%2C_in_Delhi_on_August_15%2C_2017.jpg/440px-thumbnail.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2200" data-file-height="1472" /></a><figcaption>Modi interacting with the school children after delivering his address on <a href="/wiki/Independence_Day_(India)" title="Independence Day (India)">Independence Day</a> in New Delhi, 15 August 2017</figcaption></figure>
<p>During his premiership, Modi has received consistently high approval ratings; at the end of his first year in office, he received an overall approval rating of 87% in a <a href="/wiki/Pew_Research" class="mw-redirect" title="Pew Research">Pew Research</a> poll, with 68% of respondents rating him "very favorably" and 93% approving of his government.<sup id="cite_ref-439" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-439">&#91;427&#93;</a></sup> Modi's approval rating remained largely consistent at around 74% during his second year in office, according to a nationwide poll conducted by instaVaani.<sup id="cite_ref-440" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-440">&#91;428&#93;</a></sup> At the end of his second year in office, an updated Pew Research poll showed Modi continued to receive high overall approval ratings of 81%, with 57% of those polled rating him "very favorably".<sup id="cite_ref-441" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-441">&#91;429&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-442" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-442">&#91;430&#93;</a></sup> At the end of his third year in office, a further Pew Research poll showed Modi with an overall approval rating of 88%, his highest yet, with 69% of people polled rating him "very favorably".<sup id="cite_ref-443" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-443">&#91;431&#93;</a></sup> A poll conducted by <i><a href="/wiki/The_Times_of_India" title="The Times of India">The Times of India</a></i> in May 2017 showed 77% of respondents rated Modi as "very good" and "good".<sup id="cite_ref-444" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-444">&#91;432&#93;</a></sup> In early 2017, a survey by Pew Research Center showed Modi to be the most popular figure in Indian politics.<sup id="cite_ref-445" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-445">&#91;433&#93;</a></sup> In a weekly analysis by <a href="/wiki/Morning_Consult" title="Morning Consult">Morning Consult</a> called the Global Leader Approval Rating Tracker, Modi had the highest net approval rating as of 22 December 2020 of all government leaders in the 13 countries being tracked.<sup id="cite_ref-446" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-446">&#91;434&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-447" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-447">&#91;435&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="In_popular_culture">In popular culture</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Category:Cultural_depictions_of_Narendra_Modi" title="Category:Cultural depictions of Narendra Modi">Category:Cultural depictions of Narendra Modi</a></div>
<p><i>Modi Kaka Ka Gaon</i> (Modi uncle's town), a 2017 Indian <a href="/wiki/Hindi" title="Hindi">Hindi</a>-language drama film by Tushar Amrish Goel, is the first <a href="/wiki/Biopic" class="mw-redirect" title="Biopic">biopic</a> about Modi. It stars Vikas Mahante in the titular role.<sup id="cite_ref-448" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-448">&#91;436&#93;</a></sup> <i><a href="/wiki/PM_Narendra_Modi" title="PM Narendra Modi">PM Narendra Modi</a></i>, a 2019 Hindi-language biographical drama film by <a href="/wiki/Omung_Kumar" title="Omung Kumar">Omung Kumar</a>, stars <a href="/wiki/Vivek_Oberoi" title="Vivek Oberoi">Vivek Oberoi</a> in the titular role and covers Modi's rise to the premiership.<sup id="cite_ref-449" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-449">&#91;437&#93;</a></sup> An Indian web series called <i><a href="/wiki/Modi:_Journey_of_a_Common_Man" title="Modi: Journey of a Common Man">Modi: Journey of a Common Man</a></i>, which is based on the same premise, was released in May 2019 on the <a href="/wiki/Video_streaming" class="mw-redirect" title="Video streaming">video streaming</a> platform <a href="/wiki/Eros_Now" title="Eros Now">Eros Now</a> with <a href="/wiki/Ashish_Sharma" title="Ashish Sharma">Ashish Sharma</a> portraying Modi.<sup id="cite_ref-450" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-450">&#91;438&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/7_RCR_(TV_series)" title="7 RCR (TV series)"><i>7 RCR</i></a> (<i><a href="/wiki/7,_Race_Course_Road" class="mw-redirect" title="7, Race Course Road">7, Race Course Road</a></i>), a 2014 Indian <a href="/wiki/Docudrama" title="Docudrama">docudrama</a> political television series which charts the political careers of prominent Indian politicians, covered Modi's rise to the PM's office in the episodes "Story of Narendra Modi from 1950 to 2001", "Story of Narendra Modi in Controversial Years from 2001 to 2013", "Truth Behind Brand Modi", "Election Journey of Narendra Modi to 7 RCR", and "Masterplan of Narendra Modi's NDA Govt"; with Sangam Rai in the role of Modi.<sup id="cite_ref-451" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-451">&#91;439&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/India:_The_Modi_Question" title="India: The Modi Question">India: The Modi Question</a>, a 2023 <a href="/wiki/BBC" title="BBC">BBC</a> documentary, examines Modi's role in the 2002 Gujarat riots and his record as Prime Minister of India. The Indian government banned the documentary, drawing widespread criticism.<sup id="cite_ref-452" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-452">&#91;440&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Hindu_2023_453-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Hindu_2023-453">&#91;441&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-NPR_2023_454-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NPR_2023-454">&#91;442&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-NYT_Yasir_2023_455-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NYT_Yasir_2023-455">&#91;443&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Other portrayals of Modi include those by <a href="/wiki/Rajit_Kapur" title="Rajit Kapur">Rajit Kapur</a> in the film <i><a href="/wiki/Uri:_The_Surgical_Strike" title="Uri: The Surgical Strike">Uri: The Surgical Strike</a></i> (2019) and <a href="/wiki/Vikram_Gokhale" title="Vikram Gokhale">Vikram Gokhale</a> in the web-television series <i><a href="/wiki/Avrodh:_The_Siege_Within" title="Avrodh: The Siege Within">Avrodh: The Siege Within</a></i> (2020), both of which are based on the <a href="/wiki/2016_Uri_attack" title="2016 Uri attack">2016 Uri attack</a> and the <a href="/wiki/2016_Indian_Line_of_Control_strike" title="2016 Indian Line of Control strike">subsequent Indian surgical strikes</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-456" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-456">&#91;444&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-457" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-457">&#91;445&#93;</a></sup> Gokhale reprised the role in the sequel <i><a href="/wiki/Avrodh:_The_Siege_Within_2" title="Avrodh: The Siege Within 2">Avrodh: The Siege Within 2</a></i> (2022)<i>,</i> which is based on the <a href="/wiki/2016_Indian_banknote_demonetisation" title="2016 Indian banknote demonetisation">2016 Indian banknote demonetisation</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-458" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-458">&#91;446&#93;</a></sup> Pratap Singh played a character based on Modi in <i><a href="/wiki/Chand_Bujh_Gaya" title="Chand Bujh Gaya">Chand Bujh Gaya</a></i> (2005) which is set against the backdrop of the Gujarat riots.<sup id="cite_ref-Hindu_459-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Hindu-459">&#91;447&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Modi appeared in an episode of <a href="/wiki/Discovery_Channel_India" class="mw-redirect" title="Discovery Channel India">Discovery Channel</a>'s show <i><a href="/wiki/Man_vs_Wild" class="mw-redirect" title="Man vs Wild">Man vs Wild</a></i> with the host <a href="/wiki/Bear_Grylls" title="Bear Grylls">Bear Grylls</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-460" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-460">&#91;448&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-461" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-461">&#91;449&#93;</a></sup> becoming the second world leader after Barack Obama to appear in the reality show.<sup id="cite_ref-462" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-462">&#91;450&#93;</a></sup> In the show, Modi treks through jungles, and talks about nature and wildlife conservation with Grylls.<sup id="cite_ref-463" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-463">&#91;451&#93;</a></sup> The episode was recorded in <a href="/wiki/Jim_Corbett_National_Park" title="Jim Corbett National Park">Jim Corbett National Park</a>, <a href="/wiki/Uttarakhand" title="Uttarakhand">Uttarakhand</a>, and was broadcast in India and 180 other countries.<sup id="cite_ref-464" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-464">&#91;452&#93;</a></sup> Modi hosts <i><a href="/wiki/Mann_Ki_Baat" title="Mann Ki Baat">Mann Ki Baat</a></i>, a monthly radio programme on <a href="/wiki/All_India_Radio" title="All India Radio">All India Radio</a>, and has conducted the competition <i><a href="/wiki/Pariksha_Pe_Charcha" title="Pariksha Pe Charcha">Pariksha Pe Charcha</a></i>, and discussions for students and the issues they face in examinations.<sup id="cite_ref-465" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-465">&#91;453&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-466" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-466">&#91;454&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Awards_and_recognition">Awards and recognition</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/List_of_awards_and_honours_received_by_Narendra_Modi" title="List of awards and honours received by Narendra Modi">List of awards and honours received by Narendra Modi</a></div>
<p>In March 2012 and June 2014, Narendra Modi appeared on the cover of the Asian edition of <i><a href="/wiki/Time_(magazine)" title="Time (magazine)">Time Magazine</a></i>, becoming one of the few Indian politicians to have done so.<sup id="cite_ref-467" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-467">&#91;455&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-468" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-468">&#91;456&#93;</a></sup> In 2014, <i><a href="/wiki/CNN-News18" title="CNN-News18">CNN-News18</a></i> (formally <i>CNN-IBN</i>) news network awarded Modi <a href="/wiki/CNN-News18_Indian_of_the_Year" class="mw-redirect" title="CNN-News18 Indian of the Year">Indian of the Year</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Indian_of_the_Year_of_2014_469-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Indian_of_the_Year_of_2014-469">&#91;457&#93;</a></sup> In June 2015, Modi was featured on the <a href="/wiki/List_of_covers_of_Time_magazine_(2010s)" title="List of covers of Time magazine (2010s)">cover of Time Magazine</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-470" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-470">&#91;458&#93;</a></sup> In 2014, 2015, 2017, 2020 and 2021, he was named one of Time magazine's <a href="/wiki/Time_100" title="Time 100">100 Most Influential People in the World</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-471" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-471">&#91;459&#93;</a></sup> <i><a href="/wiki/Forbes_Magazine" class="mw-redirect" title="Forbes Magazine">Forbes Magazine</a></i> ranked him the 15th Most Powerful Person in the World in 2014 and the <a href="/wiki/Forbes_list_of_The_World%27s_Most_Powerful_People" class="mw-redirect" title="Forbes list of The World&#39;s Most Powerful People">9th Most Powerful Person in the World</a> in 2015, 2016 and 2018.<sup id="cite_ref-472" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-472">&#91;460&#93;</a></sup> In 2015, Modi was ranked the <a href="/wiki/50_Most_Influential_(Bloomberg_Markets_ranking)" class="mw-redirect" title="50 Most Influential (Bloomberg Markets ranking)">13th Most Influential Person in the World</a> by <i><a href="/wiki/Bloomberg_Markets" title="Bloomberg Markets">Bloomberg Markets</a> Magazine</i>.<sup id="cite_ref-473" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-473">&#91;461&#93;</a></sup> In 2021 <i>Time</i> called Modi the third "pivotal leader" of independent India after <a href="/wiki/Jawaharlal_Nehru" title="Jawaharlal Nehru">Jawaharlal Nehru</a> and <a href="/wiki/Indira_Gandhi" title="Indira Gandhi">Indira Gandhi</a>, who "dominated the country's politics like no one since them".<sup id="cite_ref-474" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-474">&#91;462&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-475" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-475">&#91;463&#93;</a></sup> Modi was ranked fifth on <i><a href="/wiki/Fortune_(magazine)" title="Fortune (magazine)">Fortune Magazine</a></i><span class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;">&#39;</span>s first annual list of the "World's Greatest Leaders" in 2015.<sup id="cite_ref-476" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-476">&#91;464&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-477" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-477">&#91;465&#93;</a></sup> In 2017, <a href="/wiki/Gallup_International_Association" title="Gallup International Association">Gallup International Association</a> (GIA) conducted a poll and ranked Modi third-top leader of the world.<sup id="cite_ref-478" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-478">&#91;466&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-479" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-479">&#91;467&#93;</a></sup> In 2016, a wax statue of Modi was unveiled at <a href="/wiki/Madame_Tussauds" title="Madame Tussauds">Madame Tussauds</a> <a href="/wiki/Wax_museum" title="Wax museum">wax museum</a> in <a href="/wiki/London" title="London">London</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-480" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-480">&#91;468&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-481" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-481">&#91;469&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Narendra_Modi_figure_at_Madame_Tussauds_London_(33783646132).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/Narendra_Modi_figure_at_Madame_Tussauds_London_%2833783646132%29.jpg/170px-Narendra_Modi_figure_at_Madame_Tussauds_London_%2833783646132%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="227" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/Narendra_Modi_figure_at_Madame_Tussauds_London_%2833783646132%29.jpg/255px-Narendra_Modi_figure_at_Madame_Tussauds_London_%2833783646132%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/Narendra_Modi_figure_at_Madame_Tussauds_London_%2833783646132%29.jpg/340px-Narendra_Modi_figure_at_Madame_Tussauds_London_%2833783646132%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2448" data-file-height="3264" /></a><figcaption>Narendra Modi's wax statue at Madame Tussauds, London</figcaption></figure>
<p>In 2015, Modi was named one of <i>Time</i><span class="nowrap" style="padding-left:0.1em;">&#39;</span>s "30 Most Influential People on the Internet" because he was the <a href="/wiki/List_of_most-followed_Twitter_accounts" title="List of most-followed Twitter accounts">second-most-followed politician</a> on <a href="/wiki/Twitter" title="Twitter">Twitter</a> and <a href="/wiki/Facebook" title="Facebook">Facebook</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-482" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-482">&#91;470&#93;</a></sup> In 2018, he was the third-most-followed world leader on Twitter,<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (May 2023)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> and the most-followed world leader on Facebook and <a href="/wiki/Instagram" title="Instagram">Instagram</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-483" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-483">&#91;471&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-484" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-484">&#91;472&#93;</a></sup> In October 2018, Modi received United Nations' highest environmental award, the <a href="/wiki/Champions_of_the_Earth" title="Champions of the Earth">Champions of the Earth</a>, for policy leadership by "pioneering work in championing" the <a href="/wiki/International_Solar_Alliance" title="International Solar Alliance">International Solar Alliance</a> and "new areas of levels of cooperation on environmental action".<sup id="cite_ref-auto4_485-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto4-485">&#91;473&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-auto6_486-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto6-486">&#91;474&#93;</a></sup> Modi was conferred the 2018 <a href="/wiki/Seoul_Peace_Prize" title="Seoul Peace Prize">Seoul Peace Prize</a> in recognition of "his dedication to improving international co-operation, raising global economic growth, accelerating the Human Development of the people of India by fostering economic growth and furthering the development of democracy through anti-corruption and social integration efforts". He is the first Indian to win the award.<sup id="cite_ref-auto5_487-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto5-487">&#91;475&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-auto3_488-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto3-488">&#91;476&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Following his <a href="/wiki/Second_swearing-in_ceremony_of_Narendra_Modi" title="Second swearing-in ceremony of Narendra Modi">second swearing-in ceremony</a> as Prime Minister of India, a picture of Modi was displayed on the facade of the <a href="/wiki/Abu_Dhabi_National_Oil_Company" title="Abu Dhabi National Oil Company">Abu Dhabi National Oil Company</a> (ADNOC) building in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.<sup id="cite_ref-489" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-489">&#91;477&#93;</a></sup> The Texas India Forum hosted a community event in honour of Modi on 22 September 2019 at <a href="/wiki/NRG_Stadium" title="NRG Stadium">NRG Stadium</a> in <a href="/wiki/Houston" title="Houston">Houston</a>, <a href="/wiki/Texas" title="Texas">Texas</a>. The event was attended by over 50,000 people and several American politicians, including President <a href="/wiki/Donald_Trump" title="Donald Trump">Donald Trump</a>, making it the largest gathering for an invited <a href="/wiki/List_of_diplomatic_visits_to_the_United_States" title="List of diplomatic visits to the United States">foreign leader visiting the United States</a> other than the <a href="/wiki/Pope" title="Pope">Pope</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-490" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-490">&#91;478&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-491" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-491">&#91;479&#93;</a></sup> At the event, Modi was presented with the <a href="/wiki/List_of_Keys_to_the_City_in_the_United_States#Texas" title="List of Keys to the City in the United States">Key to the City</a> of Houston by Mayor <a href="/wiki/Sylvester_Turner" title="Sylvester Turner">Sylvester Turner</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-492" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-492">&#91;480&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Bill_%26_Melinda_Gates_Foundation" title="Bill &amp; Melinda Gates Foundation">Bill &amp; Melinda Gates Foundation</a> awarded Modi the <a href="/wiki/Goalkeepers_(Gates_Foundation)" title="Goalkeepers (Gates Foundation)">Global Goalkeeper Award</a> on 24 September 2019 in New York City, in recognition of the <a href="/wiki/Swachh_Bharat_Mission" title="Swachh Bharat Mission">Swachh Bharat Mission</a> and "the progress India has made in providing safe sanitation under his leadership".<sup id="cite_ref-auto2_493-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto2-493">&#91;481&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-494" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-494">&#91;482&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-auto1_495-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto1-495">&#91;483&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2020, Modi was among eight world leaders who were awarded the parody <a href="/wiki/Ig_Nobel_Prize" title="Ig Nobel Prize">Ig Nobel Prize</a> in Medical Education "for using the <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_India" title="COVID-19 pandemic in India">COVID-19 viral pandemic</a> to teach the world that politicians can have a more immediate effect on life and death than scientists and doctors can".<sup id="cite_ref-496" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-496">&#91;484&#93;</a></sup> On 21 December 2020, US President Donald Trump awarded Modi the <a href="/wiki/Legion_of_Merit" title="Legion of Merit">Legion of Merit</a> for improving <a href="/wiki/India%E2%80%93United_States_relations" title="India–United States relations">India–United States relations</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-497" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-497">&#91;485&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-498" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-498">&#91;486&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-499" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-499">&#91;487&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-500" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-500">&#91;488&#93;</a></sup> On 24 February 2021, <a href="/wiki/Gujarat_Cricket_Association" title="Gujarat Cricket Association">Gujarat Cricket Association</a> renamed Motera Stadium in <a href="/wiki/Ahmedabad" title="Ahmedabad">Ahmedabad</a>—<a href="/wiki/List_of_cricket_grounds_by_capacity" title="List of cricket grounds by capacity">the largest cricket stadium in the world</a>—<a href="/wiki/Narendra_Modi_Stadium" title="Narendra Modi Stadium">Narendra Modi Stadium</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-501" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-501">&#91;489&#93;</a></sup>
</p>

<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Writing_career">Writing career</span></h2>
<p>In 2008, Modi published a Gujarati book titled <i>Jyotipunj</i>, which contains profiles of RSS leaders. The longest was of <a href="/wiki/M._S._Golwalkar" title="M. S. Golwalkar">M. S. Golwalkar</a>, under whose leadership the RSS expanded and whom Modi refers to as <i>Pujniya Shri Guruji</i> ("Guru worthy of worship").<sup id="cite_ref-507" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-507">&#91;495&#93;</a></sup> According to <i><a href="/wiki/The_Economic_Times" title="The Economic Times">The Economic Times</a></i>, Modi's intention was to explain the workings of the RSS to his readers, and to reassure RSS members he remained ideologically aligned with them.
</p><p>After becoming the Prime Minister he also authored a book called <a href="/wiki/Exam_Warriors" title="Exam Warriors">Exam Warriors</a>, a guide for children to commendably face exams. Modi has written eight other books, mostly containing short stories for children.<sup id="cite_ref-508" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-508">&#91;496&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Private_life">Private life</span></h2>
<p>Modi used to maintain a close and publicised relationship with his <a href="/wiki/Centenarian" title="Centenarian">centenarian</a> mother, Hiraben.<sup id="cite_ref-509" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-509">&#91;497&#93;</a></sup>
</p>

<li id="cite_note-18"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-18">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">Sources stating that Modi has failed to improve human development indices in Gujarat.<sup id="cite_ref-Buncombe_11-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Buncombe-11">&#91;8&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Jaffrelot2013_12-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jaffrelot2013-12">&#91;9&#93;</a></sup></span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-lo9-39"><span class="mw-cite-backlink">^ <a href="#cite_ref-lo9_39-0"><sup><i><b>a</b></i></sup></a> <a href="#cite_ref-lo9_39-1"><sup><i><b>b</b></i></sup></a></span> <span class="reference-text">Sources describing that India has experienced a <a href="/wiki/Democratic_backsliding" title="Democratic backsliding">backslide in democracy</a>:<sup id="cite_ref-34" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-34">&#91;28&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:2_35-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-35">&#91;29&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:4_36-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:4-36">&#91;30&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-37" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-37">&#91;31&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-38" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-38">&#91;32&#93;</a></sup></span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-49"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-49">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">Sources discussing the controversy surrounding Modi.<sup id="cite_ref-Buncombe_11-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Buncombe-11">&#91;8&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-43" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-43">&#91;36&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Stepan_44-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Stepan-44">&#91;37&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Ganguly_2014_45-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Ganguly_2014-45">&#91;38&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-CBC_46-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CBC-46">&#91;39&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Robinson_47-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Robinson-47">&#91;40&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Burke_48-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Burke-48">&#91;41&#93;</a></sup></span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-85"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-85">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">Applications were filed with the <a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister%27s_Office_(India)" title="Prime Minister&#39;s Office (India)">Prime Minister's Office</a> (PMO) under the <a href="/wiki/Right_to_Information_Act,_2005" title="Right to Information Act, 2005">RTI Act</a> seeking details of his arrest. In reply, the PMO said it maintains official records on Modi only since he became the prime minister in 2014. Despite this claim, the official website of the PMO contains information about Modi from the 1950s.<sup id="cite_ref-83" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-83">&#91;75&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-84" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-84">&#91;76&#93;</a></sup></span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-96"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-96">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">Replying to an RTI query, the School of Open Learning said it did not have any data of students who received a BA degree in 1978.<sup id="cite_ref-SOL_86-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-SOL-86">&#91;77&#93;</a></sup> Jayantibhai Patel, a former political science professor of Gujarat University, said the subjects listed in Modi's MA degree were not offered by the university when Modi was studying there.<sup id="cite_ref-93" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-93">&#91;84&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-94" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-94">&#91;85&#93;</a></sup> In 2016, <a href="/wiki/Delhi_University" title="Delhi University">Delhi University</a> deemed the BA degree to be authentic.<sup id="cite_ref-95" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-95">&#91;86&#93;</a></sup></span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-124"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-124">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">The exact number of people killed in the train burning is variously reported. For example, the <a href="/wiki/BBC" title="BBC">BBC</a> says it was 59,<sup id="cite_ref-122" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-122">&#91;112&#93;</a></sup> while <i><a href="/wiki/The_Guardian" title="The Guardian">The Guardian</a></i> put the figure at 60.<sup id="cite_ref-123" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-123">&#91;113&#93;</a></sup></span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-361"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-361">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">"The Narendra Modi led government completed two years in power in May 2016 and the prime minister has made his mark on both the domestic and foreign policy fronts. It is important to assess how successful his initiatives have been in the arena of foreign affairs in comparison to his predecessors. In this regard, this paper identifies and examines the key trends and issues in foreign policy under the Modi led administration and the measures needed to translate speeches and policies into action. Modi government has also taken a serious node of relations with middle-east nations, as well as Iran and Israel."<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHall2016278–281_360-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHall2016278–281-360">&#91;349&#93;</a></sup> </span>
</li>
</ol></div>
